body:
Have you heard of the “Ship of Theseus”? When
Theseus, a famous Greek hero, ⓐreturned from his
adventure of rescuing the children of Athens, the
Athenians wanted to preserve his ship. They kept
replacing the wood pieces that had decayed until
all the original pieces were replaced with new
ⓑone. In this situation, could we still call it the
Ship of Theseus?
Well, we are living examples of the Ship of
Theseus. Every day, we are changing and growing
to become new versions of ourselves. This means
that our future selves may be very different from
ⓒwho are we now. Then how can we create a future
we’ll be proud of? I have some advice for you.
First, actively envision the kind of person who you
want to become in the future. To do this, spend
time with different kinds of people to learn more
and stay curious. Second, when ⓓexpressing your
views online or with friends, remember that your
future self might disagree with your current opinions.
So, be respectful of other people’s opinions and
don’t just assume that you are always right. Finally,
your future self will have strengths and wisdom
ⓔthat you may lack today. Even if you can’t do
something now, you might be able to in the future.
So, don’t be afraid of new challenges. Be brave!

A common misconception in science is ⓐthat only
highly trained experts can participate in research
and
data
analysis.
However,
with
the
right
opportunity, anyone can become a scientist, and
yes, that means even you! ⓑDealing with a vast
amount of data can take scientists decades, but
with the eyes, ears, and perspectives of citizen
scientists, this job can ⓒbe completed in a few
years or even just a few months. Citizen scientists
collect, classify, or analyze data ⓓso that scientists

scientific community ⓔexpanding knowledge and

Project Budburst
Most flowers bloom in spring, and many leaves
change color in autumn. Due to global warming,
however, the timing of seasonal cycles is changing.
Scientists have been trying to find out exactly how
and where these cycles are changing, as well as
how fast the changes are occurring. The problem is
that it is impossible for them to keep track of
every single plant in the country. This is where
citizen science comes in. Project Budburst is a

increase lift and jumping distance are increasing
their speed, spreading out their bodies and skis,

Whales are amazing creatures. They are enormous
and live incredibly long lives. The largest blue
whales can grow as long as 30 meters and weigh
over 200 tons, and some whales have been known
to live for more than 100 years. These giants do
extremely beneficial things for the environment
throughout their long lives and even after death.
According to scientists, a single whale can absorb
about 550 kilograms of CO₂ per year, while a tree
can absorb only 22.
Moreover, after they die, whales sink to the ocean
floor with all the CO₂ they absorbed during their
lives. Their bodies then become food and habitats
for deep-sea creatures. This process is called a
whale fall. Whale falls permanently bury about
145,000 tons of CO₂ under the sea every year. This
achievement is basically what expensive carbon
capture technologies aim to do — capture carbon
and then store it underground.

Have you heard of the “Ship of Theseus”? When Theseus, a famous Greek hero, returned from his adventure of rescuing the children of Athens, the Athenians wanted to preserve his ship. They kept replacing the wood pieces that had decayed until all the original pieces were replaced with new ones. In this situation, could we still call it the Ship of Theseus? Well, we are living examples of the Ship of Theseus. Every day, we are changing and growing to become new versions of ourselves. This means that our future selves may be very different from who we are now. Then how can we create a future we’ll be proud of? I have some advice for you. First, actively envision the kind of person you want to become in the future. To do this, spend time with different kinds of people to learn more and stay curious. Second, when expressing your views online or with friends, remember that your future self might disagree with your current opinions. So, be respectful of other people’s opinions and don’t just assume that you are always right. Finally, your future self will have strengths and wisdom that you may lack today. Even if you can’t do something now, you might be able to in the future. So, don’t be afraid of new challenges. Be brave! CO₂ through whale falls, whales also make a
significant indirect contribution to reducing CO₂
through an act called a whale pump. This refers to
the vertical movements of whales that _______________
________________________________. Whales dive deep into
the ocean to feed on prey such as krill and small
fish, and they occasionally swim up to the surface
to breathe. When they near the surface, they
release an enormous amount of waste. This waste is
rich in nutrients that are essential for creatures
living in that area. Specifically, it creates the perfect
growing conditions for some microscopic creatures
floating at the surface of the ocean.
These creatures, called phytoplankton, may look
tiny and insignificant, but when taken together, they
play a significant role in reducing CO₂. They absorb
about 40% of the carbon in the atmosphere and
produce about 50% of the atmosphere’s oxygen.
They do this through photosynthesis, a process that
creates energy using carbon, water, and light. It is
estimated that increasing the world’s phytoplankton
by 1% is equivalent to planting 2 billion new trees.
Whale pumps deliver nutrients not only to the
ocean surface but also to deeper areas of the
ocean. As whales swim back down to feed at the
ocean’s bottom, their movements stir up the water
and bring nutrients down to the creatures living
below. Whale pumps promote the growth of marine
life at various depths throughout the ocean.

Moreover, after they die, whales sink to the ocean
floor with all the CO₂ they absorbed during their
lives. Their bodies then become food and habitats
for deep-sea creatures. This process is called a
whale fall. Whale falls permanently bury about
145,000 tons of CO₂ under the sea every year. This
achievement is basically what expensive carbon
capture technologies aim to do — capture carbon
and then store it underground.
In addition to their direct absorption and burial of
CO₂ through whale falls, whales also make a
significant indirect contribution to reducing CO₂
through an act called a whale pump. This refers to
the vertical movements of whales that help circulate
nutrients across different depths of the ocean. Whales
dive deep into the ocean to feed on prey such as
krill and small fish, and they occasionally swim up to
the surface to breathe. When they near the surface,
they release an enormous amount of waste. This
waste is rich in nutrients that are essential for
creatures living in that area. Specifically, it creates the
perfect growing conditions for some microscopic
creatures floating at the surface of the ocean.
These creatures, called phytoplankton, may look
tiny and insignificant, but when taken together, they
play a significant role in reducing CO₂. They absorb
about 40% of the carbon in the atmosphere and
produce about 50% of the atmosphere’s oxygen.

Sociologists classify generations based on an
individual’s birth year. The four most recent generations
are baby boomers, Generation X, Generation Y (or
millennials), and Generation Z. Baby boomers are
named so because the birth rate was significantly
higher when they were born. But since Korea and
the U.S. experienced dramatic population increases
during different periods, their classifications of baby
boomers differ accordingly. In the U.S., baby boomers
are people born between 1946 and 1964, but in
Korea, baby boomers are those born between 1955
and 1963. Generation X (1965-1980) earned its
name from the title of a book written by Douglas
Coupland in 1991. According to the book, people in
their twenties in that era had a relaxed and
laid-back lifestyle. The following generations, born
after Generation X, were later called Y (1981-1996)
and Z (1997-2012). Members of Generation Y are
also called millennials because they became adults
with the beginning of the new millennium.
choices: How Are Generations Classified and Named?
Why Do Generational Values Change Over Time?
Why Are Generational Labels Socially Significant?
How Do Life Stages Shape Generational Identity?
How Are Generations Interpreted in ContemporarySociety?

The cohort effect and the traditional notion of a
generation are closely related. ⓐBroadly speaking,
each generation is defined by the birth years of its
members. According to the theory of generational
cohorts, individuals who belong to a particular
generation are socialized in distinct conditions
compared to other generations. They experience
similar political, economic, and social events during
their early stages of life, ⓑwhich shape their beliefs,
values, and behaviors in similar ways.
The
cohort
effect
results
in
characteristic
differences
between
generations.
For
instance,
Koreans went through the 1997 financial crisis,
ⓒalso known as the International Monetary Fund
(IMF) crisis. Gen Xers were in their 20s at that time,
and thus experienced great employment instability.
ⓓThis may have led them to prioritize secure
employment for their children. In contrast, Gen Zers
grew up with smartphones, and this earned them
the “digital natives” label. ⓔThey are accustomed to
getting their news, information, and advice from
social media. Their strength in using digital media,
however, often leads them to lack social skills.

In Greek myths, Apollo and Artemis, twin children
of Zeus and Leto, were brother and sister. They
were highly skilled in hunting and often enjoyed
going hunting together. Inspired by Apollo, the god
of the Sun, NASA named its first Moon project
after him: the Apollo Program. They aimed to hit
the “bull’s-eye” of the Moon, which was 380,000 km
away. Through this project, in 1969, Neil Armstrong
became the first person to walk on the Moon,
famously declaring, “That’s one small step for a
man, one giant leap for mankind.” The most recent
Moon landing took place in 1972, and a total of 12
astronauts have walked on the Moon. More than 50
years later, NASA declared its plan to go back to
the Moon and began the Artemis Project. Named
after Apollo’s twin sister, Artemis, the project aims
to use innovative technologies to land the first
woman and the first person of color on the Moon
in the near future. After exploring the Moon, NASA
is planning to take the next giant leap: sending the
first astronauts to Mars.

young. Remember how we used to look for the
best place for patbingsu?

choices: I can relate to you.

M: In today’s lecture, I’m going to talk about two
different ways to ask for permission in English:
“Can I ... ?” versus “Do you mind if I ... ?”
Depending on the context, you may want to
use one or the other. For example, let’s say you
want to ask your close friend if you can borrow
a pen. In this situation, you might say, “Can I
borrow your pen?” It may sound strange to say,
“Do you mind if I borrow your pen?” On the
other hand, imagine you want to sit on a bench
in a park, but someone is already sitting there.
In this situation, it’d be more appropriate to
say, “Do you mind if I sit next to you?” than
“Can I sit next to you?” This is because you’d
generally want to be more polite when you’re
talking to people you don’t know. You should
use polite or casual styles of communication
depending on who you are talking to and how
close you are to them. So, choose expressions
carefully when communicating with others.
choices: Asking for permission in English is difficult, soyou should avoid it whenever possible.
You should always use casual expressions whentalking to friends or people you know well.
Politeness in English depends only on the wordsyou choose, not on the situation or the person.
English has many ways to ask questions, and itis important to know the difference betweenthem.
When asking for permission in English, it iscrucial to choose the expression based on thesituation and the person.
solution: 영어로 허락을 요청하는 표현으로 좀 더 격의 없는 방식인 “Can I …?”와 좀 더 공손함을 나타내는 표현인 “Do you mind if I …?”가 있으며, 이 두 가지 의사소통 방식은 상대가 가까운 친구인지 공원에서 만난 모르는 사람인지에 따라 적절히 구분 해서 써야 한다는 예시를 소개하고, 다른 사람들과의 의사소통 에서 신중하게 표현을 선택하는 것이 중요하다고 결론짓고 있 으므로, 글의 요지로 ❺ ‘영어로 허락을 요청할 때, 상황과 상 대에 근거하여 표현을 선택하는 것이 중요하다.’가 알맞다. 미래엔(김성연) 2과

light pollution from satellites.

body:
In Greek myths, Apollo and Artemis, twin children
of Zeus and Leto, were brother and sister. They
were highly skilled in hunting and often enjoyed
going hunting together. Inspired by Apollo, the god
of the Sun, NASA named its first Moon project
after him: the Apollo Program. They aimed to hit
the “bull’s-eye” of the Moon, (A)[where / which] was
380,000 km away. Through this project, in 1969, Neil
Armstrong became the first person (B)[walked / to
walk] on the Moon, famously declaring, “That’s one
small step for a man, one giant leap for mankind.”
The most recent Moon landing took place in 1972,
and a total of 12 astronauts have walked on the
Moon. More than 50 years later, NASA declared its
plan to go back to the Moon and began the
Artemis Project. (C)[Named / Naming] after Apollo’s
twin sister, Artemis, the project aims to use
innovative technologies to land the first woman and
the first person of color on the Moon in the near
future. After exploring the Moon, NASA is planning
to take the next giant leap: sending the first
astronauts to Mars.

solution: (A) 콤마(,) 뒤에서 동사 was의 주어가 없는 불완전한 절(was 380,000 km away)을 이끌어 선행사인 명사구 the “bull’s-eye” of the Moon을 부연 설명하는 관계사절을 이루어야 하므로, 계속적 용법의 주격관계대명사 which가 적절하다. (B) 동사(became)가 있는 완전한 절(Neil Armstrong became the first person)에 이어지는 준동사 자리이며, 흐름상 ‘걸은 (최초의 사람)’이라는 뜻으로 명사구 the first person을 수식해 야 하므로 형용사적 용법의 to부정사 to walk가 적절하다. (C) 주절 앞에 콤마(,)와 함께 쓰여 주절 주어 the project를 부 연 설명하는 분사구문을 이루는 분사 자리로, the project가 ‘이름이 붙여진’ 대상이며 뒤에 목적어 없이 ‘name ~ after … (~을 …의 이름을 따서 짓다)’의 전치사 after와 명사구 Apollo’s twin sister, Artemis가 이어지므로, ‘~ be named after …(~가 …의 이름을 따서 지어지다)’의 과거분사 Named가 적절하다.

윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓖ 중, 어법상 어색한 것을 모두 골라 짝지은 것은?
solution: ⓐ have caused → has caused (명사구 The increasing number of satellites를 과거분사구 launched into orbit이 수식해 주어부를 이루고 있으며, 이어지 는 동사 자리에 과거부터 지금까지 ‘야기해 왔다’라는 의미로 현재완료(have[has]+p.p.)가 쓰이는 것은 적절하나, 주어의 핵심 인 number가 단수명사이므로 단수 조동사 has로 수일치 시켜 야 한다. 따라서 have caused를 has caused로 고친다.) ⓒ have launched → have been launched (주어 Enormous numbers of low-flying satellites가 복수명사 구이고, 글의 흐름상 과거부터 현재까지 ‘발사되어 온’ 것이므 로 복수 조동사(have)로 수일치한 현재완료가 쓰이는 것은 적 절하나, 주어가 ‘발사되는’ 대상이고 뒤에 목적어가 없으므로, 현재완료 능동태인 have launched를 현재완료 수동태 (have[has]+been+p.p.)인 have been launched로 고친다.) ⓔ remain → remains (주어 Approximately 37 percent of the global population에 이어지는 동사 자리에 ‘계속 ~인 상태이다’라는 뜻으로 뒤의 형용사 unconnected를 보어로 취하는 불완전자동사 remain이 쓰이는 것은 적절하나, ‘숫자+percent of+명사(구)’가 주어일 때 이어지는 동사의 수는 of 뒤의 명사(구)에 수일치 시키므로, 단 수명사구 the global population에 수일치한 단수동사를 써야 한다. 따라서 복수동사 remain을 단수동사 remains로 고친다.) ⓖ we can ensure → can we ensure (Only를 포함한 부사구가 강조를 위해 문두에 쓰였으므로 이어 지는 절의 주어와 동사를 도치시켜야 하며, 조동사가 있는 경 우 ‘부사구+조동사+주어+동사원형 ~’의 어순이 되므로 we can ensure을 can we ensure로 고친다.)

body:
(A)흔히 현대 컴퓨터 과학의 아버지로 여겨지는 Alan
Turing은 컴퓨터 메모리의 개념을 개발하고 최초로 전
자 저장 프로그램을 만든 것으로 유명했다. In 1950,
in his research paper titled “Computing Machinery
and Intelligence,” he posed a thought-provoking
question: Can machines think? This research paper
was the first to provide a framework for thinking
about machine intelligence. Turing wanted to see if
a machine could be as intelligent as humans and
asked himself, “If a machine could imitate human
behavior, why wouldn’t it be able to think like a
human?”
This question led Turing to design the “imitation
game,” which also became known as the “Turing
test.” The game itself was simple: A human
participant would exchange a series of typed
interactions with two respondents, a computer and
a human being. After a set period of time, the
participant would be asked to state which answers
came from the computer and which came from the
human being. If the participant failed to distinguish
one from the other, the computer had passed the
Turing test. It might be then inferred that the
computer had the ability to think like a human.
Turing predicted that this pattern would eventually
happen so consistently that machines would be
considered intelligent. In the early days of computer
science, he already imagined a world in which
people could build machines that could “think.”
1950: Alan Turing introduced the Turing test.
1956: The term “artificial intelligence” was coined.

choices: Turing introduced the Turing test as a practicalexperiment to improve computer performance.
Turingarguedthatmachinescouldthinkindependently of human behavior and interaction.
Turing attempted to define human intelligenceby comparing it with the operational mechanismsof machines.
Turing emphasized the technical limitations ofearly computers and questioned their ability toreplicate human intelligence.
Turing devised the Turing Test to see ifmachines could think like humans and predictedthe possibility that such machines could becreated.

Often considered the father of modern computer
science, Alan Turing was famous for developing the
idea of computer memory and making the first
design of an electronic stored program. In 1950, in
his research paper titled “Computing Machinery and
Intelligence,” he posed a thought-provoking question:
Can machines think? This research paper was the first
to provide a framework for thinking about machine
intelligence. Turing wanted to see if a machine could
be as intelligent as humans and asked himself, “If a
machine
could
imitate
human
behavior,
why
wouldn’t it be able to think like a human?”
This question led Turing to design the “imitation
game,” which also became known as the “Turing
test.” The game itself was simple: A human
participant would exchange a series of typed
interactions with two respondents, a computer and
a human being. After a set period of time, the
participant would be asked to state which answers
came from the computer and which came from the
human being. If the participant failed to distinguish
one from the other, the computer had passed the
Turing test. It might be then inferred that __________
__________________________________________________________.
Turing predicted that this pattern would eventually
happen so consistently that machines would be
considered intelligent. In the early days of computer
science, he already imagined a world in which
people could build machines that could “think.”

윗글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?
choices: the computer could store and retrieve informationefficiently
the computer might surpass human emotionalunderstanding
the computer followed logical rules designed byhumans
the computer could perform tasks faster thanhumans
the computer had the ability to think like a human
solution: ‘기계가 인간처럼 생각할 수 있는가’라는 질문은 Turing이 ‘모 방 게임’을 고안하게 만들었으며, 튜링 테스트로도 알려진 이 게임에서 참가자가 컴퓨터와 인간의 답변을 구별하지 못했다 면, 그 컴퓨터는 튜링 테스트를 통과한 것이 되었다는 내용 뒤 에 이어지므로, 이러한 결과로부터 기계가 인간처럼 생각할 수 있다는 것이 추론되었을지도 모른다는 흐름이 되어야 한다. 따 라서 빈칸에는 ❺ ‘컴퓨터가 인간처럼 생각할 수 있는 능력을 가졌다’가 알맞다.

body:
In Greek myths, Apollo and Artemis, twin children
of Zeus and Leto, were brother and sister. They
were highly skilled in hunting and often enjoyed
going hunting together. Inspired by Apollo, the god
of the Sun, NASA named its first Moon project
after him: the Apollo Program. They aimed to hit
the “bull’s-eye” of the Moon, which was 380,000 km
away. Through this project, in 1969, Neil Armstrong
became the first person to walk on the Moon,
famously declaring, “That’s one small step for a
man, one giant leap for mankind.” The most recent
Moon landing took place in 1972, and a total of 12
astronauts have walked on the Moon. More than 50
years later, NASA declared its plan to go back to
the Moon and began the Artemis Project. Named
after Apollo’s twin sister, Artemis, the project aims
to use innovative technologies to land the first
woman and the first person of color on the Moon
in the near future. After exploring the Moon, NASA
is planning to take the next giant leap: sending the
first astronauts to Mars.

윗글의 주제로 알맞은 것은?
choices: the historical influence of Greek mythology onmodern scientific research fields
the influence of NASA’s lunar exploration programson public interest in science and technology
the similarities and differences between theApollo and Artemis projects for lunar exploration
theevolutionofNASA’slunarexplorationprograms whose names were inspired by themythological figures
the challenges faced by NASA’s lunar explorationprogramsandthesolutionsdevelopedtoovercome them
solution: NASA가 그리스 신화에 나오는 태양의 신 아폴로에게서 영감 을 받아 최초의 달 프로젝트를 아폴로 프로그램이라고 이름 지었고, 1969년에 닐 암스트롱이 최초로 달에 발을 디딘 후 1972년에는 12명의 우주 비행사가 달을 밟았으며, 그로부터 50년 후 시작된 아르테미스 프로젝트는 아폴로의 쌍둥이 누나 인 아르테미스의 이름을 딴 것으로, 가까운 미래에 최초의 여 성이자 최초의 유색인종을 달에 착륙시키는 것을 목표로 하고 있다는 내용을 다루고 있으므로, 글의 주제로 ❹ ‘이름이 신화 의 인물들에서 영감을 받은 NASA의 달 탐사 프로그램들의 발 전’이 알맞다.

day.(나는 언 젠가 화성에서의 삶을 경험할 수 있으면 좋겠어.)’라고 말하며 자신의 개인적 바람을 나타내고 있으므로, 어떤 일이 이루어질 가능성에 대해 의구심을 나타내는 표현인 ② ‘내가 언젠가 화성에서의 삶을 경험을 할 수 있을지 의심스러워 보여.’로는 바꿔 쓸 수 없다. 오답 ① 내가 언젠가 화성에서의 삶을 경험할 기회를 가질 수 있다면 좋을 텐데. 관계사절을 연결한다. <보기> 의 one of 뒤에 관계대명사 which를 쓰고, one에 수일치 한 단수동사 is와 보어인 명사구 space debris를 쓴다. 16) ⑤: 위성으로 인한 빛 공해 때문에 밤하늘의 밝기가 계속 증가하여 2030년에는 자연적인 어둠보다 최대 12% 더 밝아질 것이라고 설명하므로, 이러한 빛 공해의 결과로 야기되는 문제가 구조하는 데 도움이 된다. 18) ④: NASA가 그리스 신화에 나오는 태양의 신 아폴로에게 서 영감을 받아 최초의 달 프로젝트를 아폴로 프로그 램이라고 이름 지었고, 1969년에 닐 암스트롱이 최초 로 달에 발을 디딘 후 1972년에는 12명의 우주 비행사 가 달을 밟았으며, 그로부터 50년 후 시작된 아르테미 스 프로젝트는 아폴로의 쌍둥이 누나인 과학과 기술에 대한 대중의 관심에 미친 영향 ③ 달 탐사를 위한 아폴로와 아르테미스 프로젝트 사 이의 유사점과 차이점 ⑤ NASA의 달 탐사 프로그램들이 직면했던 도전들과 그것들을 극복하기 위해 개발된 해결책들 19) (1) Neil Armstrong became the first person to walk on the Moon (2) to use innovative technologies to land the first woman and the first person of color on the Moon 질문 (1) 1969년에 아폴로 프로그램을 통해 어떤 역사적인 성취 가 이루어졌는가? → 1969년에, 닐 암스트롱은 달 위를 걸은 최초의 사람이 되었다. (2) 아르테미스 프로젝트는 가까운 미래에 무엇을 달성하는 것을 목표로 하는가? → 그것은 혁신적인 기술을 사용하여 최초의 여성과 최초 의 유색인종을 달에 착륙시키는 것을 목표로 한다. 20) ③: (A) TV 신호, 라디오, 인터넷, 전화 서비스를 지원한다는 내용이 이어지므로, 이를 통해 위성 데이터가 전 세계 통신을 용이하게 한다는 흐름으로 facilitating(용이하게 하는 것)이 알맞다. delaying 지연시키는 것 (B) 위성은 날씨 예보를 위해 데이터를 수집한다는 것 에 이어, 지구 대기와 다른 행성, 별을 탐사하는 과학 연구와 실험에도 사용된다는 내용이 언급되므로, 위성 이 널리 사용된다는 흐름으로 extensively(광범위하게)가 알맞다. sparsely 드물게 (C) 고해상도 이미지는 군사 감시를 포함한 여러 용도 로 활용된다는 내용이 이어지므로, 위성 데이터가 관측 및 모니터링 목적에도 매우 유용하다는 흐름이 되는 invaluable(매우 귀중한)이 알맞다. valueless 쓸모없는

Often considered the father of modern computer
science, Alan Turing was famous for developing the
idea of computer memory and ⓐmaking the first
design of an electronic stored program. In 1950, in
his
research
paper
ⓑwas
titled
“Computing
Machinery
and
Intelligence,”
he
posed
a
thought-provoking question: Can machines think?
This research paper was the first to provide a
framework for thinking about machine intelligence.
Turing wanted to see ⓒwhich a machine could be
as intelligent as humans and asked himself, “If a
machine
could
imitate
human
behavior,
why
wouldn’t it be able to think like a human?”
This question led Turing to design the “imitation
game,” ⓓwhat also became known as the “Turing
test.” The game itself was simple: A human
participant would exchange a series of typed
interactions with two respondents, a computer and
a human being. After a set period of time, the
participant would be asked to state which answers
came from the computer and which came from the
human being. If the participant failed ⓔdistinguishing
one from the other, the computer had passed the
Turing test. It might be then inferred that the
computer had the ability to think like a human.

deep
learning
artificial

The engineers didn’t instruct the neural network to

the images. They waited to find out if the neural

images and form classifications in an unsupervised
manner. After the neural network processed the

detect three images: a human face, a human body,
and
a
cat.

seemingly
simple
research
represented
a
significant
advancement
in
the
unsupervised image recognition tasks of neural

Often considered the father of modern computer
science, Alan Turing was famous for developing the
idea of computer memory and making the first
design of an electronic stored program. In 1950, in
his research paper titled “Computing Machinery and
Intelligence,” he posed a thought-provoking question:
Can machines think? This research paper was the first
to provide a framework for thinking about machine
intelligence. Turing wanted to see if a machine could
be as intelligent as humans and asked himself, “If a
machine
could
imitate
human
behavior,
why
wouldn’t it be able to think like a human?”
This question led Turing to design the “imitation
game,” which also became known as the “Turing
test.” The game itself was simple: A human
participant would exchange a series of typed
interactions with two respondents, a computer and
a human being. After a set period of time, the
participant would be asked to state which answers
came from the computer and which came from the
human being. If the participant failed to distinguish
one from the other, the computer had passed the
Turing test. It might be then inferred that the
computer had the ability to think like a human.
Turing predicted that this pattern would eventually
happen so consistently that machines would be
considered intelligent. In the early days of computer
science, he already imagined a world in which
__________________________________________________________.

Often ⓐconsider the father of modern computer
science, Alan Turing was famous for developing the
idea of computer memory and making the first
design of an electronic stored program. In 1950, in
his research paper titled “Computing Machinery and
Intelligence,” he posed a thought-provoking question:
Can machines think? This research paper was the
first ⓑto provide a framework for thinking about
machine intelligence. (A)Turing은 기계가 인간만큼 지
능적일 수 있는지 알아보기를 원했으며, ‘만약 기계가
인간 행동을 모방할 수 있다면, 왜 그것이 인간처럼
생각할 수 없겠는가?’라는 질문을 스스로에게 던졌다.
This question led Turing to design the “imitation
game,” which also became known as the “Turing
test.” The game itself was simple: A human
participant would exchange a series of typed
interactions with two respondents, a computer and
a human being. After a set period of time, the
participant would be asked ⓒstating which answers
came from the computer and which came from the
human being. If the participant failed to distinguish
one from the other, the computer had passed the
Turing test. ⓓIt might be then inferred that the
computer had the ability to think like a human.
Turing predicted ⓔthat this pattern would eventually
happen so consistently that machines would be
considered intelligent. In the early days of computer
science, he already imagined a world in which
people could build machines that could “think.”
1950: Alan Turing introduced the Turing test.
1956: The term “artificial intelligence” was coined.

to analyze the psychological effects of human–computer interaction in early artificial intelligenceresearch
to evaluate the practical limitations of earlycomputer systems in mimicking human intelligence
to compare the Turing Test with other methodsfor measuring artificial intelligence
to argue that machines will eventually surpasshuman intelligence
solution: 현대 컴퓨터 과학의 아버지라고 불리는 Alan Turing이 1950년 자신의 연구 논문에서 “기계가 생각할 수 있는가?”라는 질문을 제기하며 기계 지능에 대해 생각하기 위한 틀을 최초로 제공 했고, 튜링 테스트를 고안함으로써 지능을 가진 기계가 만들어 질 가능성에 대해 예측하고 상상했다는 내용으로, 인공 지능이 만들어질 가능성을 제기하고 이론적 틀을 확립한 Alan Turing 의 업적에 대해 설명하고 있으므로, 글의 목적으로 ❶ ‘인공지 능을 만들 가능성을 제기하고 그 이론적인 기반을 확립한 Alan Turing을 업적을 설명하기 위해’가 알맞다. 미래엔(김성연) 3과

(B) A network of 16,000 computer processors was

video
images
and
form
classifications
in
an
unsupervised manner. (E) This seemingly simple
research represented a significant advancement in
the unsupervised image recognition tasks of neural
networks and marked the beginning of a new era
of artificial intelligence research.
Many experts predict that artificial intelligence will
impact every aspect of 21st century life. AI will
improve the way ⓓhow we work, play, and
communicate. Along with hope and excitement,
there are also concerns. Some people argue that AI
will take our jobs and eventually control human

stroll around the charming, medieval town. Upon
arrival, the two towers of St. Kilian Cathedral
ⓑwelcome you. And within a five-minute walk of
the towers, the Würzburg Residence, a UNESCO
World Heritage Site, will be on full display with
Court Gardens and Residence Square. This beautiful
palace was built by the most ⓒprominent architects
and artists of the 18th century from Austria, France,
Italy, and Germany. But the ⓓbeauty of the city
doesn’t stop there. For a more ⓔadventurous
experience, take a stroll along the banks of the
Main and watch the sun set behind the skyline. It’s
an excellent photo spot, so I took some during the
sunset.

(C) 동사 hurried 뒤에 접속사 없이 다른 동사가 쓰일 수 없고 ‘서둘러 ~하다’라는 뜻으로 ‘hurry+to부정사’를 사용하므로, to arrange가 알맞다. 미래엔(김성연) 1과

On August 1, 1914, Ernest Shackleton departed
London on the ship Endurance with 27 men and 69
dogs to cross the Antarctic continent. (A)그들은 앞
으로의 여정이 역사상 가장 험난한 모험들 중 하나가
될 줄을 거의 알지 못했다.
The crew members were full of excitement, but
when their ship got stuck in thick pack ice on
January 18, 1915, their joy quickly turned to fear.
“Oh, my! It’s frozen like an almond in the middle of
a chocolate bar!” cried one of the crew members.
Shackleton and his men had to abandon their ship
and set up camp on the floating ice, where they
would be forced to spend the winter. Each man
was given a sleeping bag and was assigned to one
of five tents. Shackleton yielded the better sleeping
bags to other crew members and chose to stay
with the group’s more troublesome characters who
could get involved in conflicts. The camping mats
were not waterproof, so they were constantly wet.
The men shivered in the severe cold and suffered
from frostbite. Worst of all, the floating ice on
which they were camped began cracking beneath
them. Shackleton walked around inspecting the ice
regularly for the crew members’ safety. Some
nights, Shackleton and his men had to pick up their
tents, moving their camp to a more secure area
where the ice was less likely to break.

윗글의 두 번째 문단의 주제로 알맞은 것은?
choices: the Endurance’s escape from the thick pack iceunder Shackleton’s leadership
Shackleton and the Endurance crew who wereunprepared for the Antarctic expedition
how Shackleton and the Endurance crew avoidedall major dangers in the Antarctic
the anxiety and fear felt by the crew as theEndurance became trapped in thick pack ice
the Endurance stuck in thick pack ice andShackleton’s leadership during the struggle onthe ice
solution: 남극 대륙 횡단에 나선 Shackleton과 대원들이 1915년 1월 18 일 Endurance 호가 두꺼운 총빙(叢氷)에 갇히는 사건을 겪게 되어 Endurance 호를 버리고 Shackleton의 리더십 아래 대원 들이 얼음 위에서 혹독한 겨울을 나는 과정을 이야기했으므로, ❺ ‘두꺼운 총빙(叢氷)에 갇힌 Endurance 호와 얼음 위에서의 악전고투 중 Shackleton의 리더십’이 주제로 알맞다.

coining the term “a wounded healer.” He stated
that “We don’t get wounded alone, and we don’t
heal alone.” Then what does “a wounded healer”
mean? (A)상처 입은 치유자들은 그들의 고통스러운
경험이 그들로 하여금 다른 사람들을 도울 수 있게 하
는 사람들이다. They are good listeners and view all
experiences as opportunities to understand others’
hardships. Indeed, one should be wounded to
become a healer. People who go through suffering
do not always become healers. It is those who
overcome suffering who can become wounded
healers,
and
they
can
evolve
into
“wounded
leaders.” The wounded leaders are those who

who have dealt with their wounds find themselves
more at peace. Therefore, their leadership style is
characterized
by
the
ability
to
embrace
the
uncomfortable but necessary process of healing:
accepting different perspectives and focusing on
personal development while pursuing their goals.

On August 1, 1914, Ernest Shackleton (A)[departed /
reached] London on the ship Endurance with 27
men and 69 dogs to cross the Antarctic continent.
Little did they know the journey ahead would be
one of the most challenging adventures in history.
The crew members were full of excitement, but
when their ship got stuck in thick pack ice on
January 18, 1915, their joy quickly turned to fear.
“Oh, my! It’s (B)[drifting / frozen] like an almond in
the middle of a chocolate bar!” cried one of the
crew members. Shackleton and his men had to
abandon their ship and set up camp on the
floating ice, ⓐ[which / where] they would be forced
to spend the winter. Each man ⓑ[given / was
given] a sleeping bag and was assigned to one of
five tents. Shackleton yielded the better sleeping
bags to other crew members and chose to stay
with the group’s more troublesome characters who
could get involved in conflicts. The camping mats
were not waterproof, so they were constantly wet.
The men shivered in the severe cold and suffered
from frostbite. Worst of all, the floating ice on
which they were camped began (C)[cracking / freezing]
beneath them. Shackleton walked around inspecting
the ice regularly for the crew members’ safety. Some
nights, Shackleton and his men had to pick up their
tents, ⓒ[moving / moved] their camp to a more
secure area where the ice was less likely to break.

The 28 men were now isolated on drifting ice
hundreds of miles from land, with no ship, no

experiences enable them (A)__________________________.
They are good listeners and view all experiences as
opportunities
to
understand
others’
hardships.
Indeed, one should be wounded to become a
healer. People who go through suffering do not
always become healers. It is those who overcome
suffering who can become wounded healers, and
they can evolve into “wounded leaders.” The
wounded leaders are those who understand wounds
and learn from them. In fact, wounds in leadership
would be transformative because they lead to
deeper self knowledge, stronger relationships, and
greater leadership skills. Leaders who have dealt
with their wounds find themselves more at peace.

(A)흔히 현대 컴퓨터 과학의 아버지로 여겨지는 Alan
Turing은 컴퓨터 메모리의 개념을 개발하고 최초로 전
자 저장 프로그램을 만든 것으로 유명했다. In 1950,
in his research paper titled “Computing Machinery
and Intelligence,” he posed a thought-provoking
question: Can machines think? This research paper
was the first to provide a framework for thinking
about machine intelligence. Turing wanted to see if
a machine could be as intelligent as humans and
asked himself, “If a machine could imitate human
behavior, why wouldn’t it be able to think like a
human?”
This question led Turing to design the “imitation
game,” which also became known as the “Turing
test.” The game itself was simple: A human
participant would exchange a series of typed
interactions with two respondents, a computer and
a human being. After a set period of time, the
participant would be asked to state which answers
came from the computer and which came from the
human being. If the participant failed to distinguish
one from the other, the computer had passed the
Turing test. It might be then inferred that the
computer had the ability to think like a human.
Turing predicted that this pattern would eventually
happen so consistently that machines would be
considered intelligent. In the early days of computer
science, he already imagined a world in which
people could build machines that could “think.”
1950: Alan Turing introduced the Turing test.
1956: The term “artificial intelligence” was coined.

W: Jim, you seem upset. Is something wrong?
M: Yeah, my pet goldfish is sick. He’s not eating.
W: I’m sorry to hear that. I wish your goldfish were
like immortal jellyfish, which can live forever.
M: Immortal jellyfish? __________________________________
W: When it’s attacked or starved, it transforms itself
into a polyp, which is the previous life stage of
jellyfish.
M: What happens after that?
W: From the polyp, a tiny jellyfish is formed,
starting a new life cycle.
M: So, it’s like a butterfly or a chicken going back
to an egg.
W: That’s right. Immortal jellyfish can keep renewing
themselves, so they can live forever.
M: I wish my goldfish had that incredible ability!

choices: Have you seen it before?
Where did you learn about it?
Why do you think it is popular?
Can you explain how it can live forever?
How do you take care of such a special fish?

near
the
park,
a
thirteen-year-old boy ⓑnamed Richard Turere was
responsible for keeping his family’s cattle safe from
lions that often came out of the park at night to
hunt. Many neighbors had lost their cows, and
others their goats and sheep.
While ⓒrounded up his cattle one night, Richard
discovered that lions were scared of moving lights
and ⓓdidn’t come near the cattle enclosure when
he walked around carrying a flashlight. Soon, he
fastened flashing LED bulbs onto poles around the
enclosure ⓔfaced the outside and connected them
to an old car battery powered by a solar panel. He
devised the lights to flicker on and off from time
to time. It ⓕworked perfectly. After he installed his
first “lion lights,” he never spotted lions again, and
his family didn’t lose any cattle to them. Neighbors
followed suit, protecting their valuable source of
income without killing the unwanted neighbors. This
is an example of a keen observation on animal
behavior leading to a creative approach ⓖthat
brought peace and harmony.

body:
Throughout history, humans and animals have
worked together in a variety of ways. Dogs helped
round up sheep, horses and cows helped with
farming, and some animals assisted with hunting
and guarding. Raising and breeding animals has
always been a ⓐvital part of human history.
Recent studies, however, reveal there’s another
aspect to this story. It turns out that wild animals,
those that haven’t been specifically bred to live with
humans,
are
also
ⓑwilling
to
form
mutual
relationships with humans. One outstanding example
is in Laguna, Brazil, where dolphins and fishers have
teamed up to catch fish for over 130 years.
A 15-year study conducted by researchers used
drones and underwater cameras to observe this
unique
partnership.
When
ⓒmigrating
mullets
approach the shore in large groups, some dolphins
drive them towards the coast, where fishers stand
ready to catch them with their nets. The fishers watch
the dolphins, looking for them to ⓓcommunicate
that they will be making a “deep dive,” which lasts
about 15 seconds. Fishers then cast their nets just
as the dolphins drive the mullets towards the
surface.
As a result, the fishers catch much more fish, and
the dolphins get to eat mullets trying to escape
from the net. Amazingly, dolphins that engage in
this fishing are more likely to live longer, by 13
percent. Without this ⓔcompetition, dolphins may
end up swimming to areas where there aren’t many
fish, and in doing so, get caught in illegal fishing
nests.
The 130-year partnership between the dolphins
and the fishers of Laguna is more than just a way
to catch fish. It’s a win-win for both humans and
animals, a reminder of how our interactions and
relationships with the natural world can be mutually
ⓕharmful. This harmony has kept the tradition alive
for generations, and it continues to inspire us
today.

The dolphins dive deeply for about fifteenseconds to drive mullet toward the shore.
The dolphins that work with fishers tend to livelonger than those that do not.
To avoid being caught in illegal fishing nets,dolphins usually swim in areas with fewer fish.

solution: (A) 3살짜리 소녀가 자택 앞에서 코요테에게 공격당해 죽은 사 건에 대해 사람들이 격분하여 이 동물 종을 동네에서 제거하 기 위한 조치로 많은 코요테들을 죽였다는 내용 뒤에, 코요테 들이 이러한 통제 방법에 대해 의심했다는 대조적인 흐름의 내용이 연결되므로, 빈칸에는 however(그러나)가 적절하다. (B) 파괴적인 통제 방법은 번식을 막기 위해 엄격하게 인구를 통제하는 코요테 무리의 사회 구조를 붕괴시켜 개체 수 증가 를 야기한다는 내용 뒤에, 다른 먹이 동물들의 개체 수 과잉과 같이 다른 문제들을 야기할 수 있다는 또 다른 문제점이 추가 로 언급되므로, 빈칸에는 Moreover(게다가, 더욱이) 또는 In addition(게다가, 또한)이 적절하다. (C) 통제 방법을 이용해 종을 완전히 제거하는 것은 개체 수 증가를 야기하거나 다른 종의 개체 수 과잉과 같은 다른 문제 들을 야기할 수 있다는 내용을 근거로 인간이 통제를 시도할 때 자연이 어떻게 균형을 이룰지 예측하는 것은 어렵다는 명 백한 결론을 내리고 있으므로, 빈칸에는 Clearly(확실히, 분명 히) 또는 Obviously(당연히, 말할 필요도 없이)가 적절하다.

only capital with a national park, which attracts
many international tourists with wild lions and other
beasts against the backdrop of tall buildings in its
urban
center.
Living
near
the
park,
a
thirteen-year-old boy named Richard Turere was
responsible for keeping his family’s cattle safe from
lions that often came out of the park at night to
hunt. Many neighbors had lost their cows, and
others their goats and sheep.
While rounding up his cattle one night, Richard
discovered that lions were scared of moving lights
and didn’t come near the cattle enclosure when he
walked around carrying a flashlight. Soon, he
fastened flashing LED bulbs onto poles around the
enclosure facing the outside and connected them to
an old car battery powered by a solar panel. He
devised the lights to flicker on and off from time
to time. It worked perfectly. After he installed his
first “lion lights,” he never spotted lions again, and
his family didn’t lose any cattle to them. Neighbors
followed suit, ___________________________________________
_________________________________________________________.
This is an example of a keen observation on animal
behavior leading to a creative approach that
brought peace and harmony.

윗글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?
choices: depending on government assistance instead oflocal solutions
eliminating lions to permanently prevent futureattacks on livestock
reducing tourism by keeping wild animals awayfrom the national park
protecting their valuable source of income withoutkilling the unwanted neighbors
protecting their livestock by increasing fences andguards while continuing to hunt lions at night
solution: 케냐의 나이로비의 국립공원 근처에 살고 있는 소년 Richard가 사자들이 움직이는 불빛을 무서워한다는 사실을 발견하고 ‘사 자 전등’을 고안해 설치했으며, 이후 다시는 사자들을 발견하지 않았고 소를 잃지 않았다는 내용 뒤에 이웃들도 그 선례를 따 랐다고 했으며, 이것은 동물의 행동에 대한 예리한 관찰이 평 화와 조화를 가져온 창의적인 접근법으로 이어진 예라는 결론 으로 마무리되고 있으므로, 사자를 죽이는 것과 같이 파괴적인 방법을 사용하지 않고도 평화롭고 조화로운 방법으로 가축들 을 지킬 수 있었다는 흐름이 알맞다. 따라서 빈칸에 들어갈 말 로 ❹ ‘원치 않은 이웃들을 죽이지 않고도 그들의 소중한 수입 원을 보호하면서’가 적절하다.

In a suburb in the Pacific Northwest, Justin ties his
shoes for his morning run and steps out at dawn.
As he walks off his front step, he spots some
racoons crossing the street. Up in a tree, he sees a

enjoys the beauty of his neighborhood. While

In
1981,
tragic
news
shocked
Los
Angeles
residents. A three-year-old girl was attacked and
killed by a coyote in front of her home. People
were outraged and immediately took action to
remove the species from their neighborhoods. They
killed a total of 55 coyotes over a period of 80
days.
Scientists,
however,
questioned
such
a
destructive control method, as coyotes are highly
adaptive and breed quickly. A study showed that a
simulated coyote population survived indefinitely
when 70% were killed annually. This means that
killing even most of the coyotes in a population
will have no significant effect. In coyote packs, a
dominant adult pair maintains a strict structure that
prevents others from breeding and controls the
population.
Destructive
control
methods
often
disrupt this social structure, resulting in increased
populations. Moreover, completely eliminating the
species using a control method could cause other
issues such as over-population of rodents and other
small prey. Clearly, it is difficult to predict how
nature will balance itself out when humans attempt
to control.
choices: the increasing threat wild animals pose to humansafety in expanding urban neighborhoods
the importance of eliminating top predators torestore balance between humans and nature
the historical success of aggressive populationcontrol policies in reducing urban wildlife conflicts
the role of modern city planning in completelypreventing wildlife from entering human habitats
an instance of the failure of a destructive methodto control wild animals and the reasons behind it

M: Hey, Kelly. Look at the picture of a bird. What
do you think it’s eating?
W: Oh, that’s a honeyguide bird. It’s eating some
bits of the bee nest.
M: How can it do that without getting attacked by
bees?
W: Well, the bees are not there due to some help
from humans.
M: Really? Can you explain how that works?
W: Well, when a honeyguide bird sees humans in
the forest, it makes a loud noise and guides
them to bee nests.
M: Fascinating! What happens next?
W: Once they find the nest, the humans use smoke
to drive the bees away and collect the honey.
M: Ah, so that’s when the birds can access the
food without getting attacked.
W: Yes. It’s a beautiful partnership between birds
and humans!
choices: what the honeyguide bird in the picture is eating
how a honeyguide bird avoids being attackedby bees while it accesses the bee nest
what a honeyguide bird does when it spots humansin the forest
what humans do to collect the honey from thebee nest
how humans and bees collaborate with eachother
solution: 꿀잡이새들과 인간들의 협력 방식에 관해 대화하고 있으며 인 간들과 벌들의 협력에 대해서는 언급된 바가 없으므로, ❺ ‘인 간들과 벌들은 어떻게 서로 협력하는가’는 대화를 읽고 알 수 있는 내용으로 알맞지 않다.

W: Attention, visitors and residents. The amazing
season of Red Crab Migration on Christmas
Island is back, and sooner or later, millions of
red crabs will be crossing our community from
the forest to the coast to breed or lay eggs.
Their movement peaks in the early mornings
and late afternoons when it’s cooler. Thus, all
visitors and residents are asked to follow a few
guidelines from the wildlife service office during
those hours until the end of this month. First,
it’s necessary to slow down and keep the
speed limit of 30km/h in designated areas. It’s
also necessary to completely stop your vehicle
when you spot crabs on your way. And please
stay tuned to the local radio station because
some roads may be closed. Your cooperation
will ensure the crabs’ safety and allow for our
continued appreciation of their migration every
year.
choices: to compare the migration of red crabs with thatof other animals
to explain the scientific reasons why red crabsmigrate every year
to report the results of a study on red crabpopulation changes
to advertise a tourist attraction related to redcrabs on Christmas Island
to inform people about the red crab migrationand what people should do during that period

populations.

solution: (A) 명사구 a destructive control method를 수식하므로 한정사 such가 적절하다. 참고로, such는 명사구를 수식해 ‘such+a(n)+ (형용사+)가산단수명사(구)’ 또는 ‘such+(형용사+)복수명사(구)’ 어순을 이루며, 부사인 so는 형용사[분사]와 부사를 수식한다. (B) 주어가 없는 불완전한 절(prevents ~ breeding)을 이끌어 선행사인 명사구 a strict structure를 수식하는 관계사절을 이 루어야 하므로, 주격 관계대명사 that이 적절하다. 참고로, 관계 부사 where는 완전한 절을 이끈다. body:
Throughout history, humans and animals have
worked together in a variety of ways. Dogs helped
round up sheep, horses and cows helped with
farming, and some animals assisted with hunting
and guarding. Raising and breeding animals has
always been a vital part of human history.
Recent studies, however, reveal there’s another
aspect to this story. It turns out that wild animals,
ⓐthose that haven’t been specifically bred to live
with humans, are also willing to form mutual
relationships with humans. One outstanding example
is in Laguna, Brazil, where dolphins and fishers have
teamed up to catch fish for over 130 years.
A 15-year study conducted by researchers used
drones and underwater cameras to observe this
unique
partnership.
When
migrating
mullets
approach the shore in large groups, some dolphins
drive ⓑthem towards the coast, where fishers stand
ready to catch ⓒthem with their nets. The fishers
watch
the
dolphins,
looking
for
ⓓthem
to
communicate that ⓔthey will be making a “deep
dive,” which lasts about 15 seconds. Fishers then
cast their nets just as the dolphins drive the mullets
towards the surface.
As a result, the fishers catch much more fish, and
the dolphins get to eat mullets trying to escape
from the net. Amazingly, dolphins that engage in
this fishing are more likely to live longer, by 13
percent. Without this cooperation, dolphins may end
up swimming to areas where there aren’t many fish,
and in doing so, get caught in illegal fishing nests.
The 130-year partnership between the dolphins
and the fishers of Laguna is more than just a way
to catch fish. It’s a win-win for both humans and
animals, a reminder of (A)_____________________________
_______________________________________________________.
This harmony has kept the tradition alive for
generations, and it continues to inspire us today.

choices: how humans should control nature to preventcompetition for resources
how wild animals have become dependent onhuman assistance for survival
how traditional fishing methods have changedbecause of modern technology
how our interactions and relationships with thenatural world can be mutually beneficial
how humans can dominate the natural worldthrough long-term cooperation with animals
solution: 130년 이상 물고기를 잡기 위해 함께 협력해 온 브라질 라구 나의 고래와 어부들의 사례들을 제시하면서, 어부들은 훨씬 더 많은 물고기를 잡고 돌고래들은 그물에서 벗어나려는 숭어를 먹을 수 있으며, 이 어획에 참여하는 돌고래들은 13% 정도 더 오래 살 가능성이 있다고 설명하고 있으므로, 라구나의 돌고래 와 어부의 파트너십은 단순히 물고기를 잡는 방법 그 이상이 고 인간과 동물 모두에게 이익이며, 이는 인간과 동물의 협동 적인 상호작용이 서로에게 이익이 된다는 것을 상기시켜준다 는 흐름이 알맞다. 따라서 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 ❹ ‘우리의 자 연 세계와의 상호작용 및 관계가 어떻게 상호적으로 이로울 수 있는지’가 적절하다.

M: Minji, isn’t your new English teacher coming this
week from America?
W: Yes! I want to greet him in English! Is it okay if
I call him by his first name, to say “Welcome,
Marcus!”?
M: Would you do that if he were Korean?
W: Hmm... I would probably call him seonsaengnim.
M: The same goes for English. When meeting
someone for the first time, it’s polite to call
them by their title and last name.
W: I see. So you mean like “Mr. Anderson?”
M: Yes. Do that unless he gives you permission to
use his first name.
W: Thanks for letting me know. I’ll remember that
whenever I meet someone new.
M: Okay. But when a person is around your age or
younger, you can use their first name.
W: It’s somewhat similar to Korean etiquette!

Minji thinks what she has learned about theEnglish naming etiquette is different from theKorean one.

A Journey to Samoa
Samoa is a Polynesian island country, ⓐconsisting
of two main islands (Upolu and Savai’i), located in
the South Pacific. It is known for its year-round
warm
tropical
weather,
stunning
beaches,
and
gorgeous waterfalls. Samoa even served as one of
the sources of inspiration for the directors of the
movie Moana released in 2016. It is a stunning
island country ⓑin which preserves its traditions,
history, and distinct way of life.
Samoans Have No Walls
A “fale” is a traditional Samoan house, with
round-shaped thatched huts, ⓒsupported by wood
columns, but with no walls. The architecture of fale
is very well-suited to the Samoan tropical climate.
(A)그것의 옆이 개방된 구조는 공기가 자유롭게 순환
하게 하여 공간을 계속 시원하게 할 뿐만 아니라 강한
바람이 빠져나갈 수 있도록 하여 그것이 극한 날씨를
견뎌낼 수 있도록 해준다. The unique structure of
the fale mirrors the Samoan people’s values of
openness and community. Its open structure allows
people ⓓcome and go freely, creating a sense of
belonging.
Samoans Were Time Travelers
Samoa
and
American
Samoa
are
different
countries, even though they are next to each other
in the South Pacific Ocean. Although these two
countries ⓔused to being in the same time zone,
the situation completely changed in 2011. On
December 29, 2011, Samoans skipped December 30,
and went straight to December 31, ⓕjumped 24
hours into the future. This happened because the
Samoan government decided to switch sides of the
International Date Line. This was ⓖto align the time
with New Zealand, Australia, and other Asian
countries, to improve their business transactions.
Samoa is now on the opposite side of the
International Date Line from American Samoa. They
are just half an hour apart by flight, but there is a
24-hour time difference between them. If you fly
from Samoa to American Samoa, in about 30
minutes you will return to yesterday!

윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓖ 중, 어법상 알맞은 것을 모두골라 짝지은 것은?
solution: ⓑ in which → that[which] (동사 preserves의 주어가 없는 불완전한 절(preserves ~ life) 를 이끌어 선행사인 명사구 a stunning island country를 수식 하는 관계사절을 이루어야 하므로, 완전한 절 앞에 쓰이는 ’전 치사+관계대명사‘ 형태의 in which를 선행사에 어울리는 주격 관계대명사 that 또는 which로 고친다.) ⓓ come → to come (‘~가 …하게 하다’라는 뜻으로 ‘allow+목적어+목적격보어’의 5 형식 구문에 쓰일 때 allow는 목적격보어로 to부정사를 취하므 로, allows와 목적어 people에 이어진 목적격보어 자리의 동사 원형 come을 to부정사인 to come으로 고친다.) ⓔ used to being → used to be (접속사 Although의 양보 부사절에서, 주어 these two countries의 동사 used to에 이어져 ’(예전에는) ~였다(지금은 아니다)‘라는 뜻으로 과거의 상태를 나타내는 ’used to+동사원 형‘을 이루어야 하므로, being을 동사원형 be로 고친다.) ⓕ jumped → jumping (앞의 동사구(went ~ 31)에 접속사 없이 콤마(,)로만 다른 동사 구가 이어질 수 없으므로 흐름상 동시상황을 나타내는 분사구 문을 이루는 분사 형태가 되어야 한다. 주절 주어와 동일한 분 사구문의 의미상 주어 Samoans가 ‘뛰어넘은’ 주체이므로, jumped를 능동을 나타내는 현재분사 jumping으로 고친다.)

(F) (불일치) 14) ④: (A) 기업이 ‘욕구’를 창출하는 마케팅의 예시를 설명하 고 있으므로 가치를 홍보하는 것도 수요를 ‘창출하는’ 중요한 전략이라는 흐름이 자연스럽다. 기존의 존재하 는 수요를 충족(satisfy)시키는 것이 아니라 새로운 수 요를 창출한다는 의미가 되어야 하므로 create(창출하 다)가 적절하다. satisfy ~을 충족시키다 (B) 뒤에 이어지는 예시에서 환경적 대의를 지지하는 회사는 같은 대의를 중시하는 소비자의 관심을 더 끌 수 있다고 했으므로 소비자가 자신의 가치관과 ‘일치하 는’ 브랜드를 선택한다는 흐름이 자연스럽다. 따라서 aligned(일치하는)이 적절하다. conflicted 상충된 (C) 뒤에 제시된 예시 문장에서 소비자들이 줄을 서거 나 프리미엄을 지불하고 있다는 것을 사람들이 들을 때 제품에 대한 욕구는 커질 것이라고 했으므로 ‘심리’ 를 이용해 수요를 유발한다는 흐름이 자연스럽다. 따라 서 psychology(심리)가 적절하다. rationality 합리성 15) ②: ⓑ, ⓒ는 their customers(기업들의 고객)를 가리킨다. 오답 ⓐ Businesses ⓓ Businesses ⓔ Big brands ⓕ Big brands 16) marketing, data, preferences, optimize 요약문 마케팅이 오프라인에서 온라인으로 확장됨에 따라, 기업들은 특정 고객 집단에 도달하기 위해 웹사이트, 인플 루언서, 그리고 제품 배치와 같은 새로운 도구들을 사용했 으며, 소비자들의 온라인 행동에서 얻은 데이터는 그들이 소비자 선호도를 알아내고 마케팅 노력을 최적화하는 것도 가능하게 했다. 17) ①: ⓐ what → that (완전한 절(it ~ their brand)을 이끌어 동사 realized의 목적어 역할을 하는 명사절을 이루어야 하므로 what을 명사절 접속사 that으로 고친다.) 오답 ⓑ 동사 commissioned, 목적어 Warhol에 이어지는 목 적격보어 자리로, 동사 commission은 ‘commission+목 적어+to부정사(목적격보어)’의 5형식 구조로 쓰이므로 목적격보어 자리에 to create는 적절하다. ⓒ 주어 celebrity exposure가 ‘사용되는’ 대상이므로 조 동사 can 뒤에 수동태(be p.p.)가 와야 한다. 따라서 동 사원형 be와 함께 수동태를 이루는 과거분사 used는 적절하다. ⓓ ‘찾기 위해’라는 목적의 뜻을 갖는 부사적 용법의 to 부정사 to find와 등위접속사 and로 병렬 연결되므로 to를 생략한 동사원형 create는 적절하다. ⓔ 가주어 it에 상응하는 진주어 자리이므로 to부정사 to decide는 적절하다. 18) ②: (A) 뒤에 이어지는 예시 문장에서 환경적 대의를 지지 하는 회사는 같은 대의를 중시하는 소비자의 관심을 더 끌 수 있다고 했으므로 많은 소비자가 자신의 가치관과 ‘일치하는’ 브랜드를 선택한다는 흐름이 자연스럽다. 따 라서 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 적절한 것은 matches(일치한 다), fits(부합한다)이다. 본문변형 is aligned with → matches (B) 앞에서 소비자가 자신의 가치관이 무엇인지 모를 때는 심리를 이용해 수요를 유발한다고 했으므로 소비 자들이 줄을 서거나 프리미엄을 지불하고 있다는 것을 사람들이 들을 때 제품에 대한 욕구가 ‘커질 것이다’라 는 흐름이 자연스럽다. 따라서 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 적 절한 것은 intensify(강해지다), increase(증가하다)이다. 본문변형 grow → intensify 오답 ① 일치한다  감소하다 ③ 모순된다  강해지다 ④ 부합한다  감소하다 ⑤ 모순된다  증가하다

W: Leo, what is that?
M: This is my stamp collection. I’ve collected over
700 stamps so far.
W: Amazing! Why do you collect stamps?
M: Well, I like learning about historical events through
stamp designs. For example, a Gutenberg printing
press from the 15th century is printed on this stamp.
W: A Gutenberg printing press? ______________________
_____________________
M: It was an important invention that helped people
learn how to read and write.
W: How so?
M: Before the printing press, all writings and drawings
were copied by hand. Professional copyists
worked in small rooms to copy ancient books.
W: I can’t imagine how long it must have taken to
copy an entire book by hand.
M: It took days to make a single book.
W: Books were probably too expensive for ordinary
people to own long ago.
M: Right! The printing press allowed people to make
books quickly, cheaply, and in large numbers.
W: What a revolution!

위 대화의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?
choices: What makes it so special?
Did people oppose it at the beginning?
How does it affect modern education today?
What role did it play in spreading knowledge?
Why is it considered controversial among historians?
solution: 정답은 ① 이다. (해설 없음)

body:
Museums are said to be places where time is
transformed into space. Maybe that’s why people
visit them, to learn and be inspired in new ways.
Accordingly, museums are adopting new techniques
and technologies to meet the diverse demands of
visitors.
To help visitors interact with artworks and artists
in a novel, engaging way, many museums are
adopting technology to enhance the experience of
museum-goers.
The
Van
Gogh
Museum
in
Amsterdam allows visitors to virtually touch objects
and interact with the characters inside, immersing
themselves in the artworks.
Some museums are even personalizing services, as
natural language processing techniques can be
implemented into chatbots. The chatbot of the
British Museum of London explains details not only
about the exhibits but also about the facilities and
venues, in a dozen different languages.
Personalized services will continue to be an
important part of a museum visitor’s experience.
Based on an analysis of a visitors’ background and
past behavior, including the artworks, websites, or
social media sites they’ve viewed or given a “like”
to online, deep learning systems can predict and
recommend artworks they would most likely be
interested in. The National Museum of Singapore
conducted a study in 2017 on developing a deep
learning engine that can track a visitor’s gaze,
identify
what
interests
them,
recommend
personalized tours, and show them virtual objects
on
top
of
real-world
exhibits,
often
giving
interactive
quizzes
and
games
that
suit
their
interests.
To some, visiting museums and galleries may be a
way of escaping from everyday dullness. To others,
it may be a serious attempt to enter a world of
beauty,
wonder,
imagination,
and
inspiration.
Whatever their reasons are, more visitors will seek a
unique way of appreciating the exhibits, and _______
_______________________________________________.

윗글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?
choices: visitors will prefer to view passively
more innovative services will emerge
personalized services will vanish completely
technology will reduce the need for museums
museums will limit the use of modern technologies
solution: 정답은 ② 이다. (해설 없음)

From sunrise to sunset, a constant stream of messages
fills our senses. What is all the noise about? Why is
everyone trying to communicate with us? The
answer is marketing. Marketing is a business field
(A)[in which / which] businesses or organizations
attempt to identify, satisfy, and retain customers by
creating and delivering products or services that
consumers find valuable. Billboards, social media
postings, product samples at markets, and even catchy
lyrics in songs are all forms of marketing. These
activities are utilized to increase sales, but they may
also be used for other specific objectives, such as
boosting brand awareness, building customer loyalty,
or (B)[increase / increasing] market share.
[2]
While marketing in the modern world is complex,
it was much simpler in the past. Your grandparents
have probably told you how lucky (C)[you are / are
you] to have so many modern conveniences like
washing machines, televisions, and rice cookers.
Marketing was relatively simple in the past because
every household needed to clean their clothes, watch
the news, and cook food, and few companies could
make and sell products that could perform those
tasks. Print advertisements, broadcasting, door-to-door
sales, and other offline methods were cost-effective
ways to market products that people found useful.
However, marketing has dramatically changed in
present times as businesses utilize new technology,
analyze consumer behavior, and shift business strategies.

If consumers have everything they need, how can
a business grow? Businesses can use marketing to
create “wants.” For many consumers, using a particular
brand is a status symbol. To illustrate, some
celebrities become “brand ambassadors” by using a
particular product. Their fans can associate themselves
with popular celebrities by using products that they
use. In addition, promoting values is also an
important strategy to create demand. Environmental
concerns, political alignment, and lifestyle types can
influence consumer behavior, too. When faced with
a choice between brands, many consumers will choose
a brand that is aligned with their values. For
example, companies that support an environmental
cause may be more appealing for consumers who
value the same cause. When consumers do not
know what their values are, psychological strategies
like “hunger marketing” can be used, which sparks
demand by using psychology. When people hear
that consumers are standing in line or paying a
premium, __________________________________.

how brand ambassadors utilize their status toinfluence environmental causes
ways businesses use marketing to create wantsbeyond basic consumer needs
effective ways for businesses to gather feedbackthrough social media influencers
the shift in marketing focus from creatingemotional desires to fulfilling basic needs

their products to satisfy the needs of different
consumers. However, many consumers may ask
themselves whether or not they should trust a

timing of it. If a consumer understands the
message, they know they are part of the group and
some trust can be implied. Social media influencers
can also help businesses by promoting products
that they use as consumers themselves. This type of
marketing provides businesses with feedback about
what consumers want.

strategies like meme marketing and influencer
promotion, businesses can effectively build the
bond of trust with (B)____________ consumer groups.

(B)

uniformspecific

“Good things come in small packages,” they say.
Indeed, some cultures around the world appreciate
the importance of small things, often putting them
together to create amazing works of art. Often,
practical need or creative desire plays a key role in
such efforts.
Stitched Together
Patchwork,
whose
beauty
has
long
been
appreciated in many cultures across the globe, is a
type of needlework that involves sewing scraps of
fabric together to create a larger piece of art. Every
culture is proud of its own patterns, including
Koreans, who take pride in their unique style,
jogakbo. Created during the Joseon dynasty, it is a
type of traditional wrapping cloth made by stitching
small pieces of fabric into a large square or
rectangle. Frugal women did not want to waste any
fabric and found ways to reuse it. However,
jogakbo was much more than just repurposing
fabric. It often told the creator’s life story because a
finished piece contained fabric scraps from her
wedding
skirt,
her
husband’s
shirt,
and
her
children’s clothes. The practical need to repurpose
leftover patches gave birth to a novel art form.

Stitched Together
Patchwork, whose beauty has long been appreciated
in many cultures across the globe, is a type of
needlework that involves sewing scraps of fabric
together to create a larger piece of art. Every culture
is proud of its own patterns, including Koreans, who
take pride in their unique style, jogakbo. Created
during the Joseon dynasty, it is a type of traditional
wrapping cloth made by stitching small pieces of
fabric into a large square or rectangle. Frugal women
did not want to waste any fabric and found ways to
reuse it. However, jogakbo was much more than just
repurposing fabric. It often told the creator’s life
story because a finished piece contained fabric scraps
from her wedding skirt, her husband’s shirt, and her
children’s clothes. The practical need to repurpose
leftover patches gave birth to a novel art form.
The beauty of jogakbo lies in its design, which
results from stitching together patches of various
shapes, sizes, and colors in a seemingly improvised
manner. Stitching such random patches into a perfect
square or rectangle requires artistic sensitivity, a
high level of skill, careful planning, and long hours
stitching. The desire for creative excellence resulted
in harmonious combinations of patches in various
colors, shapes, and sizes, which have been compared
to modern abstract paintings, such as those of Piet
Mondrian or Paul Klee. Jogakbo was a useful activity
in which leftover pieces of cloth were transformed into
a pursuit of beauty and utility, eventually becoming
an important part of traditional Korean craft art.
choices: Patchwork, a type of sewing, is the activity inwhich pieces of fabric are stitched together tocreate a larger work of art.
Thrifty women in the Joseon Dynasty reused fabricto make jogakbo in order to avoid wasting anycloth.
A new art form like jogakbo was born from thepractical need to recycle leftover fabric pieces.
Skilled artisans can sew random fabric piecesinto perfect squares or rectangles using onlytheir natural artistic sense.
Jogakbo, recognized for its unique patterns, hasbecome an crucial part of Korea’s traditionalcraft art.

Samoa is a Polynesian island country, consisting of
two main islands (Upolu and Savai’i), located in the
South Pacific. It is known for its year-round warm
tropical weather, stunning beaches, and gorgeous
waterfalls. Samoa even served as one of the sources
of inspiration for the directors of the movie Moana
released in 2016. It is a stunning island country that
preserves its traditions, history, and distinct way of
life.
Samoans Have No Walls
A “fale” is a traditional Samoan house, with
round-shaped thatched huts, supported by wood
columns, but with no walls. The architecture of fale
is very well-suited to the Samoan tropical climate. Its
open-sided structure not only allows air to circulate
freely to keep the space cool but also allows strong
winds to pass through, enabling it to resist extreme
weather events. The unique structure of the fale
mirrors the Samoan people’s values of openness
and community. Its open structure allows people to
come and go freely, creating a sense of belonging.

the structural advantages of the “fale”
Samoan people’s values and life attitudes

Samoans Were Time Travelers
Samoa
and
American
Samoa
are
different
countries, even though they are next to each other
in the South Pacific Ocean. Although these two
countries used to be in the same time zone, the
situation completely changed in 2011.
(A) This was to align the time with New Zealand,
Australia, and other Asian countries, to improve
their business transactions. Samoa is now on
the opposite side of the International Date Line
from American Samoa.
(B) They are just half an hour apart by flight, but
there is a 24-hour time difference between
them. If you fly from Samoa to American
Samoa, in about 30 minutes you will return to
yesterday!
(C) On December 29, 2011, Samoans skipped
December 30, and went straight to December
31, jumping 24 hours into the future. This
happened because the Samoan government
decided to switch sides of the International
Date Line.

solution: 정답은 ④ 이다. (해설 없음)

Museums are said to be places where time is
transformed into space. Maybe that’s why people
visit them, to learn and be inspired in new ways.
Accordingly, museums are adopting new techniques
and technologies to meet the diverse demands of
visitors.
To help visitors interact with artworks and artists
in a novel, engaging way, many museums are
adopting technology to (A)[enrich / standardize] the
experience
of
museum-goers.
The
Van
Gogh
Museum in Amsterdam allows visitors to virtually
touch objects and interact with the characters
inside, immersing themselves in the artworks.
Some museums are even personalizing services, as
natural language processing techniques can be
implemented into chatbots. The chatbot of the
British Museum of London explains details not only
about the exhibits but also about the facilities and
venues, in a dozen different languages.
Personalized services will continue to be an
important part of a museum visitor’s experience.
Based on an analysis of a visitors’ background and
(B)[future / past] behavior, including the artworks,
websites, or social media sites they’ve viewed or
given a “like” to online, deep learning systems can
predict and recommend artworks they would most
likely be interested in. The National Museum of
Singapore conducted a study in 2017 on developing
a deep learning engine that can track a visitor’s
gaze, identify what interests them, recommend
personalized tours, and show them virtual objects
on
top
of
real-world
exhibits,
often
giving
(C)[one-way / participatory] quizzes and games that
suit their interests.
To some, visiting museums and galleries may be a
way of escaping from everyday dullness. To others,
it may be a serious attempt to enter a world of
beauty,
wonder,
imagination,
and
inspiration.
Whatever their reasons are, more visitors will seek a
unique way of appreciating the exhibits, and more
innovative services will emerge.

M: Look! This is my favorite designer’s new release.
W: It’s amazing! Isn’t that a gat the model is
wearing?
M: Yes. I’m surprised you know what a gat is.
W: When I first saw one on a Korean historical TV
show, it looked so cool that I looked it up. It’s
made of horsehair, right?
M: Right! Then, _______________________________________?
W: No, I haven’t. What’s that?
M: It’s another kind of traditional Korean hat. It
looks similar to a gat, but it’s made of bamboo
strips instead.
W: Was it only worn by men like in the TV show?
M: Yes. Back then, women didn’t usually wear hats
like a gat or paeraengi.
W: That’s very interesting. I’m going to look for a
gat online. I think it would look good on me.

위 대화의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?

have you worn a gat in public
have you seen the designer’s older works
have you bought a traditional Korean hat
have you watched another historical TV show

Indeed, some cultures around the world appreciate
the importance of small things, often putting them
together to create amazing works of art. Often,
practical need or creative desire ⓐplays a key role
in such efforts.
Stitched Together
Patchwork, whose beauty ⓑhas long appreciated
in many cultures across the globe, is a type of
needlework that involves sewing scraps of fabric
together to create a larger piece of art. Every
culture is proud of its own patterns, including
Koreans, ⓒwhich take pride in their unique style,
jogakbo. ⓓCreated during the Joseon dynasty, it is
a type of traditional wrapping cloth made by
stitching small pieces of fabric into a large square
or rectangle. Frugal women did not want to waste
any fabric and ⓔfind ways to reuse it. However,
jogakbo was much more than just repurposing
fabric. It often told the creator’s life story because a
finished piece contained fabric scraps from her
wedding
skirt,
her
husband’s
shirt,
and
her
children’s clothes. The practical need ⓕto repurpose
leftover patches gave birth to a novel art form.
solution: ⓑ has long appreciated → has long been appreciated (관계사절의 주어 역할을 하는 whose beauty가 단수이며 흐름 상 과거부터 현재까지 ‘오랫동안 인정받아 왔다’는 것을 나타내 기 위해 단수조동사(has)로 수일치시킨 현재완료 시제를 쓰고 조동사 뒤에 부사 long을 위치시킨 것은 적절하나, whose beauty가 appreciate(~의 가치[진가]를 알다)의 대상이며 뒤에 이어진 목적어가 없으므로 현재완료 능동태(have[has] p.p.)가 아니라 현재완료 수동태(have[has] been p.p.)를 사용해 has long appreciated를 has long been appreciated로 고친다.) ⓒ which → who (콤마(,) 뒤에서 주어가 없는 불완전한 절(take ~ jogakbo)을 이끌고 있으므로 계속적 용법의 주격 관계대명사 자리이며, take pride in ~(~을 자랑스럽게 여기다)의 주체인 Koreans가 관계사절이 부연 설명하는 선행사이므로, which를 사람 선행사 와 쓰이는 주격 관계대명사 who로 고친다. 참고로, 계속적 용 법으로 관계대명사 that은 쓸 수 없다.) ⓔ find → found (흐름상 주어 Frugal women이 ‘찾았다’는 의미로, 첫 번째 과 거동사구인 did not want와 등위접속사 and로 병렬 연결되어 야 하므로, find를 과거동사 found로 고친다.) 비상(홍민표) 2과

body:
Strung Together
Throughout the ages and across all cultures, there
have been small decorative objects with a hole for
threading
called
beads.
In
its
simplest
form,
beadwork can involve threading a few beads
together on a single string to make a simple
bracelet or necklace, or on a larger scale, to form
beaded
bags,
clothing,
or
even
wall-hangings.
Beadwork is ancient, evidenced by the findings of
beads dating back to the Stone Age. Back then,
people strung bones, shells, or rocks together to
hang around their neck. As cultures and societies
evolved over time, beadwork became a form of
personal expression, a symbol of social class, or
even a talisman to drive away bad luck.
Interestingly, some regions have particularly rich
traditions. The Ndebele tribe of South Africa,
ⓐ_______________, is famed for intricate dresses made
of glass beads. Different designs serve as a means
of marking different developmental stages of a
woman’s life. An unmarried girl may wear a square
apron onto which thousands of glass beads were
hand-sewn, while a married woman might wear a
five-paneled apron, along with beaded necklaces
and a beaded cape. ⓑ_______________, beadwork is
an essential aspect of many Native American
cultures. Beadwork powerfully expresses cultural
identity, reflecting a sense of continuity across
generations.

윗글의 첫 번째 단락의 요지로 알맞은 것은?
choices: Beadwork has been limited to simple jewelrysuch as necklaces and bracelets.
Beads were mainly used in ancient times asprotective objects against physical danger.
Beadwork evolved through a long history acrossdifferent cultures, playing various symbolic roles.

solution: (A) 부분들의 단순한 합보다 더 아름답고 실용적인 새로운 형태의 창조적인 작품을 만든다는 설명이 이어지므로, 작고 단순하며 중요하지 않은 물건을 이용해 큰 의미를 갖는 예술을 창조한 다는 흐름으로 insignificant(중요하지 않은, 사소한)가 적절하다. (B) The Greek philosopher(그 그리스의 철학자)는 글 초반에 언급된 플라톤을 가리키며, 그가 ‘우리의 필요가 진정한 창조자 가 될 것입니다.‘라고 말했고, 이에 대해 필요성이나 갈망에 생 기면 공동체들이 일상의 물체들을 붙여서 더 아름답고 실용적 인 작품을 창조한다고 설명하고 있으므로, 그가 모든 창의적인 것을 위한 과정은 (주변에서) 구할 수 있는 물건들의 유용성을 극대화하기 위해 시작된다는 사실을 인식했을지도 모른다는 흐름으로 maximize(~을 극대화하다)가 적절하다. (C) 문화들은 표면적으로는 달라 보일 수도 있다는 내용 뒤에 but(그러나)으로 대조적인 내용이 연결되어야 하므로, 그것들은 대개 보편적이고 본질적인 공통의 요소를 공유하는 것 같다는 흐름으로 share(공유하다)가 적절하다. 비상(홍민표) 2과

The Sainte-Chapelle in Paris, France and Nasir
al-Mulk mosque in Shiraz, Iran amaze their visitors
with brilliant glass window panels through which
astonishing light of vigorous colors penetrates. These
panels are called stained-glass windows and are
made up of colored pieces of glass assembled
together to form large windows. In Europe and the
Middle
East,
the
techniques
for
stained-glass
windows advanced quickly during the Medieval
period, when religious buildings got bigger to
accommodate more worshipers and prayers. Small
pieces of glass assembled next to one another were
not only more practical for construction but also
able to tell a story. Since most people were illiterate
at that time, the images placed on the windows
helped them understand religious messages that
they might otherwise have been unable to grasp.
Making a stained-glass window is a process in
which intricacy is required. It involves creating
durable glass sheets and staining them, cutting
them into desired shapes, and assembling them into
prepared
designs.
Each
step
requires
expert
craftspeople working together. Though originally
used in religious structures, stained-glass windows
found their way into a variety of modern buildings,
including residential homes. These little pieces are
now recognized worldwide as an important form of
creative art, whose splendor wouldn’t have been
acknowledged without ________________________________.
choices: advances in industrial technology during themodern era
public appreciation for decorative art in non-religiousspaces
formal training systems established for professionalcraftsmen
the glass artists’ desire for beauty sparked by apractical need
the influence of changing architectural trends inmodern society

M: You know what, Amy? I had to use a GPS
Navigation app to get to the new location of
the community center.
W: I didn’t know it moved. How did it work out for
you, Grandpa?
M: Well, it did get me there, but I felt somewhat
_________________________________________________.
W: I get what you mean. You don’t pay attention
to where you’re going when using GPS.
M: Exactly, but I guess I could get used to it over
time.
W: What do you think about using it more often?
M: Well, I’m not sure I want to because it made
me feel a bit lazy.
W: Lazy? In what way?
M: I became so reliant on the app that I couldn’t
remember how I arrived anywhere.
W: I’ve felt that, too. I guess that’s what happens
when we use modern technology.

위 대화의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?
choices: satisfied with my navigation ability
very familiar with my surroundings
disconnected from my surroundings
confident about my sense of direction
completely focused on the environment around me

24/7. Farmers can then determine when they should

group from the rest or spread out the fish
population to reduce density, without resorting to
harsh chemical treatments, which can harm the fish,
the

the
consumer.

be utilized for various applications and purposes.

(B) 과거에는 마케팅이 비교적 단순했다고 했으므로, 그 이유로 는 대부분의 가정이 필요로 하는 제품을 만들고 판매할 수 있 는 회사가 많지 않았다는 흐름이 자연스럽다. 즉, 소수의 기업 만이 이러한 제품을 공급할 수 있었기 때문에 경쟁이 지금보 다 덜 복잡했을 것이고, 따라서 마케팅도 비교적 단순했을 것 이라고 볼 수 있으므로, few(거의 없는)가 적절하다. (C) 앞에서 과거에는 모든 가정이 세탁, 뉴스 시청, 요리 등을 해야 했기 때문에 필요한 제품이 거의 동일했고, 이러한 제품 을 생산하여 판매하는 기업이 거의 없었다고 했으므로 마케팅 경쟁 또한 치열하지 않았을 것으로 볼 수 있으며, 따라서 인쇄 광고, 방송, 방문 판매 및 기타 오프라인 방식은 ‘비용 효율적’ 이었다는 흐름이 자연스러우므로 cost-effective(비용 효율적인) 가 적절하다. 비상(홍민표) Special Unit 2

객관식(선다형) 1. ④ 2. ⑤ 3. ① 4. ⑤ 5. ② 6. ⑤ 7. 주관식 8. ③ 9. ① 10. ③ 11. 주관식 12. ④ 13. ③ 14. ② 15. ⑤ 16. ② 17. 주관식 18. ④ 정답 및 해설 ┃1회┃ 1) ④: 마케팅은 소비자에게 가치 있는 제품이나 서비스를 제공 하여 고객을 식별하고, 만족시키고, 유지하려는 비즈니스 분야이며, 매출 증가와 브랜드 인지도 및 고객 충성도 향상 등을 목표로 하고 다양한 형태로 이루어지는 활동 이라는 것이 핵심 내용이므로 이 글의 주제로 적절한 것 은 ④ ‘마케팅의 정의, 목적, 그리고 다양한 형태‘이다. 오답 ① 우리의 논리적 의사결정을 방해하는 소음으로서의 마 케팅 ② 디지털 시대에서 마케팅 도구의 역사적 발전 ③ 기업의 생존을 위한 필수 요소로서의 마케팅 ⑤ 기업들이 고객 충성도를 구축하기 위한 효과적인 방 법들 2) ⑤: 마케팅 활동은 브랜드 인지도 신장, 고객 충성도 구축 또는 시장 점유율 확대를 위해서도 사용될 수 있다고 했으므로 ⑤ ‘모든 마케팅 활동은 매출을 늘리는 것이라 는 유일한 목적을 위해 수행된다.‘는 일치하지 않는 내 용이다. 오답 ① 개인들은 해가 뜰 때부터 질 때까지 다양한 유형의 정보에 계속적으로 노출된다. ② 마케팅은 가치 있는 고객들을 찾고 유지하는 것을 추구하는 비즈니스 분야이다. ③ 기업들은 소비자들이 유익하다고 여길 제품이나 서 비스를 전달한다. ④ 마케팅은 소셜 미디어 게시물 그리고 심지어 노래 가사와 같은 다양한 형태를 취할 수 있다. 3) ①: (A) While은 '~인 반면, ~이지만'의 의미를 지닌 대조의 접속사이므로, 뒤에서 과거에는 마케팅이 훨씬 더 단순 했다고 한 것과 대비되어 현대의 마케팅은 '복잡하다'는 흐름이 자연스러우므로 complex(복잡한)가 적절하다. easy 쉬운 (B) 과거에는 마케팅이 비교적 단순했다고 했으므로, 그 이유로는 대부분의 가정이 필요로 하는 제품을 만들고 판매할 수 있는 회사가 많지 않았다는 흐름이 자연스럽 다. 즉, 소수의 기업만이 이러한 제품을 공급할 수 있었 기 때문에 경쟁이 지금보다 덜 복잡했을 것이고, 따라서 마케팅도 비교적 단순했을 것이라고 볼 수 있으므로, few(거의 없는)가 적절하다. numerous 많은 (C) 앞에서 과거에는 모든 가정이 세탁, 뉴스 시청, 요리 등을 해야 했기 때문에 필요한 제품이 거의 동일했고, 이러한 제품을 생산하여 판매하는 기업이 거의 없었다고 했으므로 마케팅 경쟁 또한 치열하지 않았을 것으로 볼 수 있으며, 따라서 인쇄 광고, 방송, 방문 판매 및 기타 오프라인 방식은 ‘비용 효율적’이었다는 흐름이 자연스러 우므로 cost-effective(비용 효율적인)가 적절하다. costly 값비싼 4) ⑤: ⓔ create → creating (완전한 절(a clothing company ~ jackets)과 접속사 없이 콤마(,)로만 연결되므로 분사구문 을 이루는 분사 자리이며, 의미상 주어인 a clothing company가 새로운 고객을 ‘창출하는’ 주체이므로 create 를 능동의 의미를 갖는 현재분사 creating으로 고친다.) 오답 ⓐ 비교급 more의 수식을 받아 2형식 동사 became에 이어지는 주격보어 자리이므로, 주어 the Internet and technology의 상태를 나타내는 형용사 available은 적절 하다. ⓑ 완전한 절(these ~ their brand)을 이끌어 동사 discovered의 목적어 역할을 하는 명사절을 이루고 있으 므로 명사절 접속사 that은 적절하다. ⓒ 콤마(,) 뒤에 형용사 informative와 병렬되어 뒤에 이 어지는 명사 content를 수식하므로 형용사 relevant는 적 절하다. ⓓ 조동사 could에 이어지는 동사원형 understand와 등 위접속사 and로 병렬 연결되므로 동사원형 optimize는 적절하다. 5) ②: 차례대로 F-T-F-T-T이다. (A) 온라인 마케팅이 보편화됨에 따라, 인터넷과 기술은 더 널리 사용되게 되었다.(→인터넷과 기술이 더 널리 사 용됨에 따라 온라인 마케팅이 보편화되었다.) (F) (불일치) (B) 대형 브랜드들은 자사 웹사이트를 통해 자사 제품에 대한 정보를 제공해야 한다는 것을 깨달았다.
