(B) 목적어가 없는 불완전한 절(businesses use)을 이끌 어 선행사 the strategies를 수식하는 관계사절을 이루 어야 하므로 관계대명사 that이 적절하다. (C) 선행사 ‘the video ~ recommendations’를 수식하는 관계사절의 동사 자리로, ‘the video ~ recommendations’ 가 우리에게 ‘보여지는’ 대상이므로 수동태 are shown 이 적절하다. 11) it’s up to the consumer to decide what to believe : • ‘가주어-진주어’ 구문과 ‘up to ~(~에게 달려있는)’를 사 용하여 ‘결정하는 것은 소비자에게 달려 있다’를 단어 수 에 맞춰 영작해야 하므로, 가주어 it과 be동사 is를 축약 한 it’s를 먼저 쓰고 up to the consumer(소비자에게 달 려 있는)와 진주어 to decide를 차례대로 쓴다. • decide의 목적어인 ‘무엇을 믿을지’를 영작하기 위해 ’ 의문사+to부정사‘ 구문을 활용하여 의문사 what 뒤에 to believe를 이어 쓴다. 12) ④: ⓐ 끊임없는: 규칙적으로 또는 항상 일어나는 ⓑ ~을 유지하다: 무언가를 간직하고 있거나 계속 가지 고 있다 ⓔ 집집마다 방문하는: 한 집에서 다음 집으로 오답 ⓒ 충성도: 특히 책이나 노래가 다른 사람들에게 판매 되거나 사용될 때마다 작가나 음악가에게 지급되는 돈 (→the quality of being loyal to a particular company or brand(특정 회사나 브랜드에 대해 충성스러운 특성)) ⓓ 편의용품[시설]: 어떤 것이 하기 쉽거나 접근하기 쉽 다는 사실 (→something that is useful because it saves you time or means that you have less work to do(당신의 시간 을 절약해 주거나 당신이 해야 할 일이 줄어드는 것을 의미하기 때문에 유용한 것)) 13) ③: (A) 뒤에 동사 is가 있으므로 주어 역할을 하는 동명사 using이 적절하다. (B) 접속사 When 뒤에 주어와 동사가 없으므로 분사구 문을 이루는 분사 자리이며, 의미상 주어인 many consumers가 선택에 직면한 주체이지만, 동사 face는 전치사 with와 함께 ‘be faced with ~(~에 직면하다)’의 형태로 수동태로 쓰이므로 be동사가 생략된 과거분사 구 faced with를 이루는 과거분사 faced가 적절하다. 능동 의미의 facing은 타동사로 바로 목적어를 취하므 로 뒤에 전치사 with가 올 수 없다. (C) 주어가 없는 불완전한 절(sparks ~ psychology)을 이끌어 콤마(,) 앞에 선행사 “hunger marketing”을 부연 설명하는 계속적 용법의 관계사절을 이루어야 하므로 계속적 용법의 관계대명사 which가 적절하다. 14) ②: ⓐ 앞에서 욕구를 창출하는 마케팅의 첫 번째 예로 유 명인이 특정 제품을 사용하고 팬들 또한 그 제품을 사 용함으로써 유명인과 자신을 연상시키게 하는 전략을 설명하고, 뒤에서 욕구를 창출하는 마케팅의 예로 가치 를 홍보하는 전략을 추가로 제시하고 있으므로 In addition(또한), Besides(게다가)가 적절하다. ⓑ 앞에서 브랜드들 사이에서 선택에 직면할 때 많은 소비자가 자신의 가치관과 일치하는 브랜드를 선택할 것이라고 했고, 환경적 대의를 지지하는 회사가 같은 대의를 중시하는 소비자의 관심을 더 끌 수 있다는 구 체적인 예시가 빈칸 뒤에 제시되므로 For example(예 를 들어), For instance(예를 들어)가 적절하다. 오답 ① 결과적으로 요컨대 ③ 그러므로 즉 ④ 게다가 다시 말해 ⑤ 그럼에도 불구하고 예를 들어 15) ⑤: 주어진 문장은 ‘예를 들어, John이 겨울 재킷에 대한 온 라인 리뷰를 계속 읽는다면 의류 회사는 그에게 재킷 쿠폰을 보내 새로운 고객을 창출할 수 있다.’라는 의미 로, 구체적인 사례를 제시하는 문장이다. 따라서 이 문 장 앞에는 소비자의 온라인 행동을 분석하여 개인 맞춤 형 마케팅을 수행한다는 일반적인 설명이 와야 한다. (E) 앞에서 소비자의 온라인 행동 데이터를 분석함으로 써 기업이 소비자의 선호를 더 잘 이해하고 마케팅 활 동을 최적화할 수 있다는 일반적 원리를 설명하고 있으 므로 이러한 포괄적 설명 뒤에 그 원리를 실제로 보여 주는 주어진 문장이 자연스럽게 이어진다. 따라서 주어 진 문장이 들어갈 알맞은 곳은 (E)이다. 16) ②: 인터넷과 기술을 이용할 수 있게 되면서 마케팅이 온라 인으로 확장되었다고 언급했을 뿐, 온라인 마케팅과 오 프라인 마케팅을 비교하진 않았으므로 ② ‘비용 측면에 서 온라인 마케팅은 전통적인 오프라인 마케팅과 비교 해 얼마나 효과적인가?‘는 답할 수 없는 질문이다. 오답 ① 무엇이 마케팅이 오프라인에서 온라인으로 확장되게 만들었는가? (→인터넷과 기술이 더 널리 이용 가능해 짐으로써) ③ 소셜 미디어 플랫폼에서 인플루언서들은 마케팅에 어떻게 기여하는가? (→인플루언서는 소셜 미디어 플랫 폼을 활용해 잠재 고객 및 커뮤니티와 소통함으로써 마 케팅에 기여한다.) ④ 타깃 시청자의 측면에서 스트리밍 서비스는 방송 텔 레비전과 어떻게 다른가? (→스트리밍 서비스는 방송 텔레비전보다 더 특정한 시청자와 연결할 수 있다.) ⑤ 온라인 연결의 부수적인 이점은 무엇이며, 기업들은 그것을 어떻게 활용하는가? (→부수적인 이점은 데이터 이며, 기업들은 소비자의 온라인 행동 데이터를 분석하 여 소비자 선호를 더 잘 이해하고 마케팅 전략을 최적 화한다.) 17) needs, trust, personalized, feedback 요약문 기업들이 다양한 소비자 요구를 충족시키려고 노력 함에 따라, 그들은 개인화된 경험을 제공함으로써 소비자들 과의 신뢰를 구축하기 위해 밈 마케팅을 사용하고, 한편 인 플루언서 마케팅은 소비자들이 원하는 것에 대한 피드백을 얻는 데 도움을 준다. 18) ④: 지문 앞부분에서 특정 브랜드의 사용이 곧 '지위의 상 징'이라고 언급했으므로 유명인이 특정 제품의 홍보대 사로 나설 때, 팬들은 그 제품을 사용함으로써 자신과 유명인을 연결 짓게 되고, 결과적으로 소비자들은 제품 사용을 통해 해당 유명인과 유사한 지위를 공유한다는 흐름이 자연스럽다. 따라서 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 적절한 것은 ④ ‘인기 있는 유명인과 자신을 연상시킬 수 있다 ‘이다. 오답 ① 자신이 좋아하는 유명인들과 직접 소통할 수 있다 ② 브랜드와는 별개로 자신만의 고유한 정체성을 강화 한다 ③ 제품의 환경적 영향에 대해 비판적으로 되다 ⑤ 제품의 실용적인 기능에 집중한다

solution: (A) ‘연결했던’ 주체가 주어 he이므로, 과거동사 fastened와 등 위접속사 and로 병렬 연결되어야 한다. 따라서 과거동사 connected가 적절하다. (B) 앞의 동사구 followed suit에 접속사 없이 콤마(,)로만 다른 동사구가 연결될 수 없으므로 분사구문을 이루는 분사 형태가 되어야 하며, 주절 주어와 동일한 분사구문의 주어 Neighbors 가 ‘보호하는’ 주체이고 뒤에 목적어인 명사구 their valuable source of income이 이어지므로, 능동을 나타내는 현재분사 protecting이 적절하다. Nairobi, Kenya is unique because it is the world’s
only capital with a national park, which ⓐattracts
many international tourists with wild lions and other
beasts against the backdrop of tall buildings in its
urban center. Living near the park, a thirteen-year-old
boy named Richard Turere was responsible for
keeping his family’s cattle safe from lions that often
came out of the park at night to hunt. Many
neighbors had lost their cows, and others their
goats and sheep.
While ⓑrounding up his cattle one night, Richard
discovered that lions were scared of moving lights
and didn’t come near the cattle enclosure when he
walked around carrying a flashlight. Soon, he
fastened flashing LED bulbs onto poles around the
enclosure facing the outside and connected (A)them
to an old car battery powered by a solar panel. He
devised the lights to ⓒflicker on and off from time
to time. It worked perfectly. After he installed his
first “lion lights,” he never spotted lions again, and
his family didn’t lose any cattle to (B)them. Neighbors
ⓓfollowed suit, protecting their valuable source of
income without killing (C)the unwanted neighbors.
This is an example of a keen observation on animal
behavior leading to a creative ⓔapproach that
brought peace and harmony.

윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ의 영영풀이로 알맞지 않은 것은?
choices: ⓐ attract: to make someone or something comesomewhere or take part in something
ⓑ round ~ up: to force someone or somethingto leave
ⓒ flicker: (of a light or a flame) to keep goingon and off as it shines or burns
ⓓ follow suit: to do the same as someone elsehas done
ⓔ approach: a method of doing something ordealing with a problem
solution: ⓑ ‘round ~ up’은 ‘~을 모아들이다’라는 뜻이나 ‘to force someone or something to leave(누군가나 어떤 것을 강제로 떠나게 하다)’는 ‘drive ~ out(~을 쫓아내다[내몰다])’과 같은 표현에 대한 설명이므로, ‘to find and gather together a group of people, animals, or things(한 무리의 사람들, 동물들이나 사물들을 찾아서 모으다)’와 같은 설명으로 고쳐야 한다.

body:
Throughout history, humans and animals have
worked together in a variety of ways. Dogs helped
round up sheep, horses and cows helped with
farming, and some animals assisted with hunting
and guarding. Raising and breeding animals has
always been a vital part of human history.
Recent
studies,
(A)_____________,
reveal
there’s
another aspect to this story. It turns out that wild
animals, those that haven’t been specifically bred to
live with humans, are also willing to form mutual
relationships with humans. One outstanding example
is in Laguna, Brazil, where dolphins and fishers have
teamed up to catch fish for over 130 years.
A 15-year study conducted by researchers used
drones and underwater cameras to observe this
unique
partnership.
When
migrating
mullets
approach the shore in large groups, some dolphins
drive them towards the coast, where fishers stand
ready to catch them with their nets. The fishers
watch
the
dolphins,
looking
for
them
to
communicate that they will be making a “deep
dive,” which lasts about 15 seconds. Fishers then
cast their nets just as the dolphins drive the mullets
towards the surface.
(B)_____________, the fishers catch much more fish,
and the dolphins get to eat mullets trying to
escape from the net. Amazingly, dolphins that
engage in this fishing are more likely to live longer,
by 13 percent. Without this cooperation, dolphins
may end up swimming to areas where there aren’t
many fish, and in doing so, get caught in illegal
fishing nests.
The 130-year partnership between the dolphins
and the fishers of Laguna is more than just a way
to catch fish. It’s a win-win for both humans and
animals, a reminder of how our interactions and
relationships with the natural world can be mutually
beneficial. This harmony has kept the tradition alive
for generations, and it continues to inspire us
today.

Throughout history, humans and animals have
worked together in a variety of ways. Dogs helped
round up sheep, horses and cows helped with
farming, and some animals assisted with hunting
and guarding. Raising and breeding animals has
always been a vital part of human history.
Recent
studies,
(A)_____________,
reveal
there’s
another aspect to this story. It turns out that wild
animals, those that haven’t been specifically bred to
live with humans, are also willing to form mutual
relationships with humans. One outstanding example
is in Laguna, Brazil, where dolphins and fishers have
teamed up to catch fish for over 130 years.
A 15-year study conducted by researchers used
drones and underwater cameras to observe this
unique
partnership.
When
migrating
mullets
approach the shore in large groups, some dolphins
drive them towards the coast, where fishers stand
ready to catch them with their nets. The fishers
watch
the
dolphins,
looking
for
them
to
communicate that they will be making a “deep
dive,” which lasts about 15 seconds. Fishers then
cast their nets just as the dolphins drive the mullets
towards the surface.
(B)_____________, the fishers catch much more fish,
and the dolphins get to eat mullets trying to
escape from the net. Amazingly, dolphins that
engage in this fishing are more likely to live longer,
by 13 percent. Without this cooperation, dolphins
may end up swimming to areas where there aren’t
many fish, and in doing so, get caught in illegal
fishing nests.
The 130-year partnership between the dolphins
and the fishers of Laguna is more than just a way
to catch fish. It’s a win-win for both humans and
animals, a reminder of how our interactions and
relationships with the natural world can be mutually
beneficial. This harmony has kept the tradition alive
for generations, and it continues to inspire us
today.

greener, inviting more wild animals. (C) In addition,

perfect place for feeding, mating, and nesting. (D)

to humans but to wild animals.

Predators living in cities pose serious dangersthat make urban environments unsafe for residents.

M: Hey, Kelly. Look at the picture of a bird. What
do you think it’s eating?
W: Oh, that’s a honeyguide bird. It’s eating some
bits of the bee nest.
(A) M: Fascinating! What happens next?
W: Once they find the nest, the humans use
smoke to drive the bees away and collect
the honey.
(B) M: How can it do that without getting attacked
by bees?
W: Well, the bees are not there due to some
help from humans.
(C) M: Ah, so that’s when the birds can access the
food without getting attacked.
W: Yes. It’s a beautiful partnership between
birds and humans!
(D) M: Really? Can you explain how that works?
W: Well, when a honeyguide bird sees humans
in the forest, it makes a loud noise and
guides them to bee nests.
solution: 사진을 보며 꿀잡이새가 벌집의 일부분을 먹고 있다고 말하는 주어진 대화에 이어, 대명사 that으로 그 동작을 가리켜 벌의 공격을 받지 않고 먹을 수 있는 이유에 대해 궁금해 하자 인 간의 도움으로 거기에 벌들이 없다고 답하는 (B), 대명사 that 으로 인간의 도움으로 벌이 없는 것을 가리켜 어떻게 그렇게 되는지 설명해 달라고 요청하고, 꿀잡이새가 인간들을 발견하 면 큰 소리를 내어 그들을 벌집으로 안내한다고 설명하는 (D), 그런 다음에 어떤 일이 일어나는지 궁금해 하고, 인간들이 연 기를 이용해 벌을 내쫓고 꿀을 채집한다고 설명하는 (A), 접속 사 so(그래서)로 결과를 연결하고 대명사 that으로 인간들이 연기로 벌을 내쫓고 꿀을 채집한 것을 가리켜 그때 새들이 공 격받지 않고 먹이에 접근할 수 있다고 한 뒤 새들과 인간의 아름다운 파트너십이라고 마무리짓는 (C)로 이어지는 것이 적 절하다.

agricultural fields in Asia and Europe. The idea

human safety and the well-being of the animals,

proper understanding of their behavior as well as
their role in their natural habitat. After all, we
should acknowledge the fact that both humans and
animals are temporary tenants of this precious
planet. Neither is less valuable nor more valuable
than (C)[another / the other]. Maintaining balance
and harmony among all living species is the only
choice.

Nairobi, Kenya is unique because it is the world’s
only capital with a national park, which attracts
many international tourists with wild lions and other
beasts against the backdrop of tall buildings in its
urban
center.
Living
near
the
park,
a
thirteen-year-old boy named Richard Turere was
responsible for keeping his family’s cattle safe from
lions that often came out of the park at night to
hunt. Many neighbors had lost their cows, and
others their goats and sheep.
While rounding up his cattle one night, Richard
discovered that lions were scared of moving lights
and didn’t come near the cattle enclosure when he
walked around carrying a flashlight. Soon, he
fastened flashing LED bulbs onto poles around the
enclosure facing the outside and connected them to
an old car battery powered by a solar panel. He
devised the lights to flicker on and off from time
to time. It worked perfectly. After he installed his
first “lion lights,” he never spotted lions again, and
his family didn’t lose any cattle to them. Neighbors
followed suit, protecting their valuable source of
income without killing the unwanted neighbors. This
is an example of a keen observation on animal
behavior leading to ___________________________________
_________________________________.
choices: a traditional farming practice passed downthrough generations
a government-led conservation program designedto control wild predators
an expensive technological system requiringprofessional management

Unexpected Neighbors
In a suburb in the Pacific Northwest, Justin ties his
shoes for his morning run and steps out at dawn.
As he walks off his front step, he spots some
racoons crossing the street. Up in a tree, he sees a
family of squirrels. Birds begin to sing, and he
enjoys the beauty of his neighborhood. While
running, a dangerous sight interrupts the idyllic
scene. A coyote watches as a black bear searches
through a garbage bin for food. Justin is surprised
at his neighborhood transforming into a place full
of wildlife encounters.
Why Animals Migrate to Cities
In 2019, it was estimated that more than 1.5
million
squirrels
were
living
in
Chicago
and
approximately 10,000 foxes in London. In Seoul, 155
wild boars were captured in 2022. Why are there so
many animals in big cities? One reason is that
many cities are built on biologically fertile and
productive land areas, which are attractive not only
to humans but to other creatures as well. Another
reason is due to _______________________________________
___________________________. Cities have begun building
more gardens, parks, and legally protected areas for
educational,
recreational,
or
other
purposes,
attracting more wild creatures. In addition, for some
animal species, cities have become a perfect place
for feeding, mating, and nesting. Peregrine falcons,
for example, use tall buildings for nesting sites,
man-made lighting to hunt for prey at night, and
warm urban air currents to soar easily. Cities have
become home, sweet home, not only to humans
but to wild animals.
To some, living among animals might sound idyllic,
but to others, wild animals near residential areas,
especially those predators high up in the food
chain, can be an annoyance and a threat. What
could be an optimal approach to dealing with these
new neighbors? Is there a solution for humans and
animals to live together peacefully in their shared
habitat?

urban areas becoming noisier, driving wildanimals away
natural areas becoming protected, reducinganimal movement

In
1981,
tragic
news
shocked
Los
Angeles
residents. A three-year-old girl was attacked and
killed by a coyote in front of her home. People
were outraged and immediately took action to
remove the species from their neighborhoods. They
killed a total of 55 coyotes over a period of 80
days.
Scientists,
however,
questioned
such
a
destructive control method, as coyotes are highly
adaptive and breed quickly. A study showed that a
simulated coyote population survived indefinitely
when 70% were killed annually. This means that
killing even most of the coyotes in a population
will have no significant effect. In coyote packs, a
dominant adult pair maintains a strict structure that
prevents others from breeding and controls the
population.
Destructive
control
methods
often
disrupt this social structure, resulting in increased
populations. Moreover, completely eliminating the
species using a control method could cause other
issues such as over-population of rodents and other
small prey. Clearly, (A)it is difficult to predict how
nature will balance itself out when humans attempt
to control.

Nature always returns to balance when humansapply strict control methods.
Human control over nature usually producesclear and predictable results.
Nature can be fully managed if humansunderstand ecological systems well enough.
Nature does not follow human intentions, andhasty control may lead to unexpected outcomes.

body:
Throughout history, humans and animals have
worked together in a variety of ways. Dogs helped
round up sheep, horses and cows helped with
farming, and some animals assisted with hunting
and guarding. Raising and breeding animals has
always been a vital part of human history.
Recent studies, however, reveal there’s another
aspect to this story. It turns out that wild animals,
those that haven’t been specifically bred to live with
humans,
are
also
willing
to
form
mutual
relationships with humans. One outstanding example
is in Laguna, Brazil, where dolphins and fishers have
teamed up to catch fish for over 130 years.
A 15-year study conducted by researchers used
drones and underwater cameras to observe this
unique
partnership.
When
migrating
mullets
approach the shore in large groups, some dolphins
drive them towards the coast, where fishers stand
ready to catch them with their nets. The fishers
watch
the
dolphins,
looking
for
them
to
communicate that they will be making a “deep
dive,” which lasts about 15 seconds. Fishers then
cast their nets just as the dolphins drive the mullets
towards the surface.
As a result, the fishers catch much more fish, and
the dolphins get to eat mullets trying to escape
from the net. Amazingly, dolphins that engage in
this fishing are more likely to live longer, by 13
percent. Without this cooperation, dolphins may end
up swimming to areas where there aren’t many fish,
and in doing so, get caught in illegal fishing nests.
The 130-year partnership between the dolphins
and the fishers of Laguna is more than just a way
to catch fish. It’s a win-win for both humans and
animals, a reminder of how our interactions and
relationships with the natural world can be mutually
beneficial. This harmony has kept the tradition alive
for generations, and it continues to inspire us
today.

How Modern Technology Has Completely ChangedTraditional Fishing Methods

A Win-win Partnership Between Dolphins and Fishersin Laguna Showing Human-Nature Coexistence

(A) Justin의 동네는 목가적인 분위기를 만드는 다람쥐 나 새들과 같은 야생 동물들이 있지만, 흑곰들과 같은 위험한 동물들도 있다. (T) (B) 시카고, 런던, 서울과 같은 대도시에서 야생 동물들 의 수는 눈에 띄게 감소했다. (→ 2019년에는 시카고에 150만 마리 이상의 다람쥐가, 런던에는 약 1만 마리의 여우가 살고 있는 것으로 추정되었으며, 서울에서는 2022년에 155마리의 멧돼지가 포획되었다.) (F) (C) 많은 야생 동물들이 비옥하고 생산성 있는 토지를 찾아 대도시로 온다. (T) (D) 대도시들은 야생 동물들의 생활 터전을 확보하기 위해 정원, 공원, 법적인 보호 구역들을 늘리고 있다. (→ 도시들은 교육, 오락 또는 다른 목적을 위해 더 많 은 정원, 공원, 그리고 법적인 보호 구역을 건설하기 시 작했으며, 이것이 더 많은 야생 동물들을 유인했다.) (F) (E) 야생 동물들과 도시에서 함께 살아가는 것에 대해 사람들은 엇갈리는 의견들을 가지고 있다. (T) 15) ⑤: 코요테를 죽이는 파괴적인 통제 방법은 번식을 통제하 는 코요테 무리의 엄격한 사회 구조를 붕괴시켜 개체 수 증가를 야기하고, 설치류나 다른 피식 동물의 과잉 과 같은 다른 문제들도 야기할 수 있다고 했으므로, 자 연은 인간의 예상대로 작용하지 않으며, 인간의 통제는 의도와는 다른 결과를 낳고 오히려 생태계의 균형을 무너뜨릴 수도 있다는 결론을 도출할 수 있다. 따라서 밑줄 친 (A) ‘인간이 통제를 시도할 때 자연이 어떻게 균형을 이룰지 예측하는 것은 어렵다’가 의미하는 바로 ⑤ ‘자연은 인간의 의도를 따르지 않으며, 성급한 통제 는 예상치 못한 결과로 이어질 수 있다.’가 적절하다. 오답 ① 신중한 인간의 계획은 자연의 균형을 통제하는 것 을 쉽게 만든다. ② 인간이 엄격한 통제 방법을 적용할 때 자연은 항상 균형 상태로 되돌아간다. ③ 자연에 대한 인간의 통제는 보통 명확하고 예측 가 능한 결과를 낳는다. ④ 인간이 생태계를 충분히 잘 이해한다면 자연은 완 전히 관리될 수 있다. 16) ③: 어린 소녀가 자택 앞에서 코요테에게 공격을 당해 죽은 비극적인 사건 이후 사람들이 코요테 종을 제거하기 위 해 많은 코요테를 죽였지만 큰 효과가 없었으며, 그 이 유에 대해 이러한 파괴적인 통제 방법은 코요테 무리의 사회 구조를 붕괴시켜 개체 수 증가를 야기하고, 설치 류나 다른 피식 동물의 개체 수 과잉과 같은 다른 문제 들도 야기할 수 있다고 설명하는 내용이므로, 글의 제 목으로 ③ ‘코요테를 죽여 개체 수를 통제하려는 시도 가 결국 실패한 이유’가 적절하다. 오답 ① 코요테는 어떻게 도시의 지역에서 가장 위험한 포식 자가 되었는가 ② 도시에서 야생 동물들에 대한 인간의 두려움과 폭력 적 대응의 역사 ④ 과학자들과 지방 정부에 의해 개발된 성공적인 야생 동물 통제 방법 ⑤ 코요테를 제거하는 것이 도시의 설치류 개체 수에 미치는 즉각적인 그리고 장기적인 영향 17) Balanced, Humans, Wild Animals 제시문 인간들과 야생 동물들 사이의 평화로운 공존에 대 한 균형 잡힌 시각의 필요성 18) ⑤: 인간과 야생 동물들의 상호 관계를 형성한 사례 중 하 나로 브라질의 라구나에 있는 돌고래와 어부들의 130 년 이상의 물고기를 잡기 위한 협력에 대해 소개하며, 이는 인간과 자연과의 상호 작용 및 관계가 어떻게 서 로에게 이로울 수 있는지를 상기시켜 주는 사례라고 설명하고 있으므로, 글의 제목으로 ⑤ ‘인간-자연의 상 생을 보여주는 라구나의 돌고래들과 어부들 간의 서로 에게 도움이 되는 협력 관계’가 적절하다. 오답 ① 브라질 해안가 지역의 어부들과 야생 돌고래 사이 의 갈등 ② 현대 기술이 전통적인 어업 방식에 완전히 변화를 가져온 방식 ③ 동물의 가축화의 역사와 인간 사회에서 그것의 중 요성 ④ 돌고래가 다른 동물들보다 더 지능적이라는 것을 입증하는 과학적 연구 19) ②: ‘그러나 이러한 태도 때문에 종종 의도치 않은 결과가 발생한다.’라는 역접의 연결어 However(하지만)에 의해 부정적으로 전환된 뜻의 주어진 문장은 ‘이러한 태도 (this attitude)’가 가리키는 내용, 즉 야생 동물들이 제 거되어야 할 골칫거리나 위협이라는 생각이 세계 여러 지역에서 흔하다고 언급하는 문장 뒤이자, 의도치 않은 결과가 발생할 수 있는 문제점에 대해 인간의 안전과 동물의 복지 사이에서 균형 잡힌 접근법이 필요하다는 해결책을 제시하는 문장 앞인 (B)에 들어가는 것이 적 절하다. 20) ③: 요약문 코요테 한 마리가 주거 지역에서 어린 아이를 죽인 비극적인 사건 이후, 사람들은 그 종을 (A)제거하 려고 시도했으나, 이러한 파괴적인 통제 방법은 코요테 무리의 사회적인 구조를 파괴하여 개체 수를 (B)늘리고 심지어 추가적인 부작용들도 야기한다. 오답 ① 제거하다 줄이는 ② 기르다, 사육하다 줄이는 ④ 먹이를 주다 안정시키는 ⑤ 훈련시키다 증가시키는

solution: ⓐ 주어가 전치사구(with ~ capabilities)의 수식을 받는 단수명사 구 A computer system이므로, 단수동사로 수일치한 is가 알맞다. ⓑ 콤마(,) 뒤에서 주어가 없는 불완전한 절(can ~ consumer) 을 이끌어 앞의 명사구 harsh chemical treatments를 부연 설 명하는 관계사절을 이루므로 계속적 용법의 주격 관계대명사 which가 알맞다. 참고로, ‘전치사+관계대명사’ 뒤에는 완전한 절이 이어져야 한다. ⓒ 조동사 can에 연결되는 동사원형이 올 자리이며, 주어 all this data from cameras and sensors가 타동사 utilize(~을 활 용하다)의 대상이고 뒤에 이어진 목적어가 없으므로, 수동태 be utilized가 알맞다.

body:
AI continues to advance in aquaculture to extend
beyond caged fish.
(A) Swarm robots, or many small robots working
together, can swim in and around seaweed
farms to collect data and then make decisions
on how to deal with problems that arise. Single
larger robots or even humans may be available
to take care of the physical labor from
removing harmful weeds to harvesting; however,
swarm robots may be more efficient and
cost-effective.
(B) In particular, smart fish farming technologies can
be applied to seaweed farming. Seaweed is as
ⓐ[a valuable source / valuable a source] of
food as fish. It’s also a source of fuel and an
important ingredient for cosmetics, fertilizers,
and other medicinal and industrial products.
(C) As such, ongoing research is exploring various ways
ⓑ[which / that] AI can help in the seaweed
industry, including the use of autonomous
underwater vehicles (AUVs) and swarm robotics.
Using cameras and sensors, AUVs can do many
of
the
analytical
and
diagnostic
tasks
on
seaweed farms.
The potential of AI in aquaculture is vast, and it
brings a more sustainable and technologically driven
future for fish and seaweed farming. Families that
gather together, eagerly ⓒ[anticipate / anticipating]
a healthy seafood dinner, may not be aware of the
carefully monitored fish and seaweed farms or the
cutting-edge AI technology involved in getting food
to their table. However, the process of doing so is
evidence of the considerable amount of investment
in sustainable, high-quality aquaculture with AI.
㉠With AI as an ally, the future of the oceans and
the nourishment of humanity is just a little bit more
secure.

solution: ⓐ ‘as ~ as …(…만큼 ~한)’의 원급 비교 구문을 이루는 부사 as 뒤에서 부정관사 a(n) 앞에 형용사가 위치해 ‘as+형용사 +a(n)+명사’ 어순으로 쓰이므로, as 뒤에 형용사 valuable과 관 사 a, 명사 source가 이어지는 순서의 valuable a source가 알 맞다. ⓑ 뒤에 완전한 절(AI ~ industry)을 이끌어 선행사 various ways를 수식하는 관계사절을 이루고 있으므로, 관계부사 대용 의 that이 알맞다. 참고로, 선행사 way(s)와 관계부사 how는 함께 쓰지 않고 둘 중 하나면 쓰며, 선행사 뒤에 how 대신 관 계부사 대용의 that이나 선행사에 어울리는 전치사를 사용한 ’ 전치사+관계대명사‘ 형태의 in which를 쓸 수 있다. ⓒ Families를 선행사로 하는 주격 관계대명사 that이 이끄는 절에서 동사구 gather together 다음에 접속사 없이 콤마(,)로 만 이어져 있으므로 ’eagerly ~ dinner’는 흐름상 동시동작을 나타내는 분사구문의 형태가 되어야 한다. 관계사절의 선행사 와 동일한 분사구문의 의미상 주어 Families가 ’기대하는‘ 주체 이므로 능동을 나타내는 현재분사 anticipating이 알맞다.

were pessimistic, which were ⓒidentical to the real
responses. It turns out that participants do not
make bad impressions but make better impressions
than they think.
The researchers coined a new term, the “liking
gap,” for this difference in perception or the
ⓓmismatch between how we perceive ourselves and
what others actually think of us. How is this helpful
for you? We often underestimate ourselves based
on our assumption of how others might judge us.
In other words, our ⓔflexible attitudes may prevent
us from reaching our true potential. Don’t worry
about the impression you think you make on
people; chances are you can be confident that the
impression you make is just ⓕfine.

body:
During New York Fashion Week 2018, a woman
with a brightly decorated prosthetic leg proudly
walked the runway at a major fashion show. She
was Mama Cax, a model and influencer.
Cax was diagnosed with cancer at age 14 and lost
her right leg at 16 after surgery. At first, Cax was
depressed and struggled to accept her new body.
However, with the support of her family and
friends, Cax learned to love it. One day when she
was 26, Cax posted a picture on social media
showing her leg. “I didn’t think it could help
anyone,” she said in an interview, “But after
receiving messages of support, I realized my story
could inspire others.” After receiving support from
others, she began to use social media to share
more about her life and to inspire others. She
proudly posted pictures of herself wearing stylish
prosthetic covers and spoke out about body
positivity and fashion. In 2016, she became the first
model for the #RunwayForAll campaign. In 2018,
she appeared on the cover of major fashion
magazines.
When asked, “How did you come to embrace
yourself?” she replied, “The truth is, like many
people, I’m still on my journey to self-love. There
are many barriers ahead.” In addition to modeling,
Cax showed her ability to overcome physical
barriers
by
swimming,
playing
basketball,
and
mountain climbing. She even finished the New York
City Marathon in a wheelchair.
Sadly, Mama Cax’s journey was cut short in 2019.
Although she is no longer with us, her journey will
remain in our hearts, inspiring us to (A)______________
__________________________________________________________.

윗글의 빈칸 (A)에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?
choices: develop strengths in various fields
create healthier habits to maintain physical health
pay more attention to and respect people withdisabilities
overcome limitations and find our own paths tosuccess and happiness
dress appropriately and act in a proper mannerto make good impressions on others
solution: 정답은 ④ 이다. (해설 없음)

London Transport Workers Study
In the busy London streets of 1953, a special study
was conducted. Scientists observed more than 31,000
people who had various jobs on buses and trains.
Some jobs demanded lots of moving around, like
ticket collectors, while others, like drivers, didn’t
require much movement. What was interesting was
that the workers with more active jobs had fewer
heart problems than those who sat a lot. This implied
that jobs requiring more moving around were healthier
for workers than those jobs that didn’t. What could
account for the difference in their health outcomes?

Most of the energy the body uses each day is set
or ⓐfixed. Assuming an energy input of 2,000
calories, about 1,400 calories, or 70%, goes to
essential functions such as keeping the heart and
the brain ⓑworking; this is called the basal
metabolic rate (BMR). Around 200 calories, or 10%,
is used to consume and ⓒabsorbs energy from
food and is called the thermic effect of food (TEF).
In short, BMR and TEF are the minimum energy
ⓓrequired for the body to stay alive. The remaining
400 calories, or 20%, is used for things people
choose to do, including various physical activities
(PA) like working, playing, and moving around.
Maybe some of the London public transportation
workers
spent
the
remaining
20%
differently,
ⓔresulted in their different health outcomes.

(A) About seventy percent of daily energy is used
to keep the body’s vital organs functioning. (T/F)
(B) The thermic effect of food refers to the energy
spent digesting and absorbing nutrients. (T/F)
(C) Basal metabolic rate and TEF together represent
the minimum energy for survival. (T/F)
(D) The amount of energy consumed for our physical
activities is about 10 percent. (T/F)
(E) Differences in how people used their remaining
energy may have influenced their health results. (T/F)

called Non-Exercise Activity Thermogenesis (NEAT)

completely, but not everyone has 40 minutes a day
to go for a run. Taking 10,000 steps, which is like
walking about 8 kilometers, burns 400 calories as
well. What this means is that while a 40-minute run
will burn 400 calories, doing small things like more
walking, taking stairs, or even just cleaning your
room can add up at the end of the day, too.

Then, what do people do with the remaining 400
calories? They may be burned by intense physical
exercise like jogging, working out at the gym,
playing badminton or tennis, or venturing out for a
hike. However, those calories may also be burned
by small, seemingly unimportant activities we do
throughout the day, like standing up and sitting
down, walking around the house, washing dishes,
doing the laundry, taking out the garbage, and
many others. These actions are collectively called
Non-Exercise Activity Thermogenesis (NEAT) as they
use up energy too! For example, a 40-minute run
will burn around 400 calories. Doing this could use
up the excess energy budget completely, but not
everyone has 40 minutes a day to go for a run.
Taking 10,000 steps, which is like walking about 8
kilometers, burns 400 calories as well. What this
means is that while a 40-minute run will burn 400
calories, doing small things like more walking,
taking stairs, or even just cleaning your room can
______________________________________________.
Each gram of body fat contains about 9 calories,
so if you spend your day eating and not moving,
your body may convert the 400 calories into 44
grams of fat. This is not healthy over the long
term. While NEAT doesn’t provide the heart and
muscles with the same benefits that exercise does,
excess energy still gets used up instead of being
stored. You may not necessarily get fit, but you’ll
stay in energy balance, which is important for long
term health.

(C) NEAT는 에너지를 소모하는 행위이므로 더 많이 걷기, 계단 이용하기, 물 컵을 더 자주 채우기 위해 더 작은 물 컵 사용하 기 등은 모두 에너지를 ‘사용한다’는 흐름이 자연스럽다. 따라 서 uses(사용하다)가 적절하다. 비상(홍민표) Special Unit 1

body:
The answer to this requires a simple formula and
a little bit of math. The formula is an easy
equation: the total energy expenditure of the body
equals 「BMR + TEF + PA」. In the human body, the
energy from different foods people eat is used to
keep
everything
running
smoothly.
The
basal
metabolic rate (BMR) is a measurement of how
much energy is needed to stay alive; the thermic
effect of food (TEF) is a measurement of the energy
used to consume and absorb energy from food;
and physical activity (PA) is a measurement of the
energy (A)[using / used] beyond just lying in bed.
Learning about the composition of these three
elements can help people make better choices for
their health and well-being.
Most of the energy the body uses each day is set
or fixed. Assuming an energy input of 2,000 calories,
about 1,400 calories, or 70%, goes to essential
functions such as keeping the heart and the brain
(B)[to work / working]; this is called the basal
metabolic rate (BMR). Around 200 calories, or 10%, is
used to consume and absorb energy from food and
is called the thermic effect of food (TEF). In short,
BMR and TEF are the minimum energy required for
the body (C)[stays / to stay] alive. The remaining 400
calories, or 20%, is used for things people choose to
do, including various physical activities (PA) like
working, playing, and moving around. Maybe some
of the London public transportation workers spent
the remaining 20% differently, resulting in their
different health outcomes.

다음 글의 요지로 알맞은 것은?

In the busy London streets of 1953, a special
study was conducted. Scientists observed more than
31,000 people who had various jobs on buses and
trains. Some jobs demanded lots of moving around,
like ticket collectors, while others, like drivers, didn’t
require much movement. What was interesting was
that the workers with more active jobs had fewer
heart problems than those who sat a lot. This
implied that jobs requiring more moving around
were healthier for workers than those jobs that
didn’t. What could account for the difference in
their health outcomes?
Most of the energy the body uses each day is set
or fixed. Assuming an energy input of 2,000 calories,
about 1,400 calories, or 70%, goes to essential
functions such as keeping the heart and the brain
working; this is called the basal metabolic rate (BMR).
Around 200 calories, or 10%, is used to consume and
absorb energy from food and is called the thermic
effect of food (TEF). In short, BMR and TEF are the
minimum energy required for the body to stay alive.
The remaining 400 calories, or 20%, is used for
things people choose to do, including various
physical activities (PA) like working, playing, and
moving around. Maybe some of the London public
transportation workers spent the remaining 20%
differently, resulting in their different health outcomes.
choices: Since BMR accounts for the largest portion oftotal energy expenditure, differences in BMRmay lead to different health outcomes.
How the remaining energy is used for physicalactivity explains the health differences amongLondon transport workers.
Increasing the thermic effect of food (TEF) is moreeffective for health than increasing physical activity.
The portion of energy used for physical activity remainsconstant regardless of occupation or environment.
Reducing daily calorie intake can prevent healthissues even with decreased physical activity.
solution: 런던 교통 근로자들을 대상으로 한 연구에서, 많이 움직여야 하는 직업을 가진 근로자들이 오래 앉아 있는 직업을 가진 근로자들보 다 심장 질환이 적었다는 사실이 밝혀졌고, 그 이유를 총에너지 소비량 구조에서 찾고 있다. 전체 에너지 중 BMR과 TEF처럼 생존 에 필요한 고정된 에너지를 제외하면 약 20%가 개인의 신체 활 동에 사용되는데, 이 남은 에너지를 어떻게 활용하느냐에 따라 건 강 결과가 달라질 수 있다는 내용의 글이므로, 이 글의 요지로 가 장 적절한 것은 ❷ ‘신체 활동을 위해 남는 에너지를 어떻게 사용 하는지가 런던 교통 근로자들의 건강 차이를 설명한다.’이다.

다음 글의 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 알맞게 연결된 것은?

In the big picture, your body is like an energy
account book that needs to be balanced. All the
food you eat is credit in the account, and you
need to (A)____________ energy to keep it all in
balance. Thus if you eat too much food without
using the excess energy, your body will store the
extra as fat, which is not (B)____________. Remember,
standing uses more energy than sitting, walking
uses more energy than standing, and running uses
more energy than walking, so let’s all keep moving,
stay active, and use our energy wisely for a
healthier life!
(A)              (B)

expend  unhealthy
consume  harmful
spend  healthy
preserve  good

(C) 콤마 뒤에, 목적어 역할을 하는 세 개의 완전한 절 (standing ~ sitting, walking ~ standing, and running ~ walking)만 이어지고 있으므로, 주어 없이 동사원형으 로 시작하는 명령문의 형태(Remember, 완전한 절 ~(명 심하라[기억해 두어라], ~라는 것을))가 되어야 한다. 따 라서 동사원형 Remember가 적절하다. 9) adopting a lifestyle that maximizes NEAT is a good habit for younger people to make : • ‘NEAT를 극대화하는 생활 방식을 채택하는 것’을 영작하 기 위해 adopt를 동명사로 변형하고 adopting의 목적어 a lifestyle을 이어 쓴다. a lifestyle 뒤에 주격 관계대명사 that, 동사 maximizes, 목적 NEAT를 차례대로 이어 써서 a lifestyle을 수식하는 관계사절을 완성한다. • ‘젊은 사람들이 들이기에 좋은 습관이다’를 영작하기 위 해 주어의 핵심 adopting에 이어지는 동사 is와 주격보어 a good habit를 차례대로 쓴다. a good habit을 수식하는 형용사적 용법의 to부정사 to make를 이어 쓰고, to make 바로 앞에 의미상 주어 for younger people을 쓴다. 10) ㉠ sitting time ㉡ maintain ㉢ Body ㉣ Credit ㉤ Excess 제시문 [1] NEAT의 건강상 이점 • ㉠앉아 있는 시간을 줄임으로써 심장 질환과 근손실의 위험을 감소시킴 NEAT의 일상 습관들 • 에너지 균형을 ㉡유지하는 방법으로 권장됨 [2] 에너지 장부 비유 • ㉢신체 = 에너지 장부책 • 당신이 섭취하는 음식 = 계좌에서의 ㉣수입 • 움직임 = 계좌에서의 지출 결과 및 조언 ㉤과잉 에너지 → 지방으로 저장됨 • 더 건강한 삶을 위해 활동적으로 지내기 11) ④: (A) 전치사 of의 목적어 the energy를 수식하는 분사 자리이며 the energy가 ‘사용되는’ 대상이므로 수동의 의미인 과거분사 used가 적절하다. (B) keeping의 목적어 the heart and the brain에 이어 지는 목적격 보어자리로, keep은 ‘keep+목적어+-ing(… 가 계속 ~하게 하다)’의 5형식 구조로 쓰이므로 현재분 사 working은 적절하다. (C) 앞에 의미상 주어 for the body가 있으므로 to stay가 적절하다. 12) BMR, TEF, fixed[set], health outcomes 요약문 신체의 총에너지 소비는 BMR, TEF, 그리고 PA로 구성되며, 80%를 차지하는 BMR과 TEF는 대부분 고정되어 [정해져] 있는 반면, 사람들이 남은 20%를 어떻게 사용하는 지의 차이가 그들의 건강 결과에 영향을 미칠 수 있다. 13) ④: 주어진 문장은 ‘이는 더 많이 움직여야 하는 직업이 그 렇지 않은 직업보다 근로자의 건강에 더 좋다는 것을 암시했다.’라는 뜻으로 이 문장 앞에는 더 많이 움직이 는 그룹이 그렇지 않은 그룹보다 건강 지표가 더 좋게 나타났다는 내용이 와야 한다. (D) 앞에서 활동적인 노 동자들이 심장 문제가 더 적었다는 연구 결과가 제시되 었고, 이것을 주어진 문장에서 This로 이어받아 움직이 는 직업이 더 건강하다는 결론을 제시하고 있으므로 주 어진 문장이 들어갈 알맞은 곳은 (D)이다. 14) ①: 운동만큼의 강도는 아니더라도, 일상 속 사소한 움직임 인 NEAT를 누적하는 것은 운동에 버금가는 에너지를 소비함으로써 신체의 에너지 균형과 장기적인 건강을 유지하는 데 중요한 역할을 한다는 것이 핵심 내용이므 로 ① ‘NEAT를 축적하는 것이 일일 에너지 소비와 균 형에 미치는 중요한 영향’이다. 오답 ② 칼로리를 소모하는 것만으로는 체중을 감량하기가 어 려운 이유 ③ 지방 감소를 위한 NEAT와 고강도 운동 사이의 비교 ④ 에너지 균형을 위해 당신의 일일 칼로리 섭취를 줄이 는 방법 ⑤ 왜 당신의 몸이 과잉 에너지를 지방으로 저장하는지 15) ②: (A) 앞에서 하루 종일 먹고 움직이지 않으면 신체는 400칼로리를 44g의 지방으로 전환할 수 있다고 했고, NEAT를 통해서 과잉 에너지는 ‘저장되는’ 대신에 소모 된다는 흐름이 자연스럽다. 따라서 stored(저장된)가 적절하다. released 방출된 (B) 앞에서 NEAT에 주의를 기울이면 다른 건강상의 이 점도 있다고 했으므로 NEAT를 ‘늘리는’ 생활 방식을 택하는 것이 좋은 습관이 된다는 흐름이 자연스럽다. 따라서 increases(늘리다)가 적절하다. decrease 줄이다 (C) NEAT는 에너지를 소모하는 행위이므로 더 많이 걷기, 계단 이용하기, 물 컵을 더 자주 채우기 위해 더 작은 물 컵 사용하기 등은 모두 에너지를 ‘사용한다’는 흐름이 자연스럽다. 따라서 uses(사용하다)가 적절하다. accumulate 축적하다 16) ②: 런던 교통 근로자들을 대상으로 한 연구에서, 많이 움 직여야 하는 직업을 가진 근로자들이 오래 앉아 있는 직업을 가진 근로자들보다 심장 질환이 적었다는 사실 이 밝혀졌고, 그 이유를 총에너지 소비량 구조에서 찾 고 있다. 전체 에너지 중 BMR과 TEF처럼 생존에 필요 한 고정된 에너지를 제외하면 약 20%가 개인의 신체 활동에 사용되는데, 이 남은 에너지를 어떻게 활용하느 냐에 따라 건강 결과가 달라질 수 있다는 내용의 글이 므로, 이 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은 ② ‘신체 활동 을 위해 남는 에너지를 어떻게 사용하는지가 런던 교 통 근로자들의 건강 차이를 설명한다.’이다. 오답 ① BMR이 총에너지 소비에서 가장 큰 비중을 차지하 므로, BMR의 차이가 서로 다른 건강 결과를 초래할 수 있다. ③ 식이성 발열 효과(TEF)를 증가시키는 것이 신체 활 동을 증가시키는 것보다 건강에 더 효과적이다. ④ 신체 활동에 사용되는 에너지의 비중은 직업이나 환경과 관계없이 일정하게 유지된다. ⑤ 신체 활동이 감소하더라도 일일 칼로리 섭취를 줄 이면 건강 문제를 예방할 수 있다. 17) ②: ⓑ burning → burns (주어인 동명사구 Taking 10,000 steps를 부연 설명하는 관계사절(which ~ 8 kilometers) 이 이중 콤마(,)로 주어와 동사 사이에 삽입된 형태로, 문장의 동사 자리이다. 따라서 주어인 동명사구는 단수 취급하므로 이에 수일치하도록 burning을 단수동사 burns로 고친다.) 오답 ⓐ 목적어가 없는 불완전한 절(we ~ the day)을 이끌 어 선행사 small, seemingly unimportant activities를 수식하는 관계사절을 이루고 있으므로 목적격 관계대 명사 that은 적절하다. *ⓐ는 목적격 관계대명사로 원래 지문에서 생략되었음 ⓒ 완전한 절(while ~ too)을 이끌어 be동사 is에 이어 지는 주격보어 역할을 하는 명사절을 이끌고 있으므로 명사절 접속사 that은 적절하다. ⓓ 전치사구 instead of에 이어지는 목적어 자리이며, 의미상 주어인 excess energy가 ‘저장되는’ 대상이므로 동명사의 수동태(being+p.p.) being stored는 적절하다. ⓔ 콤마(,) 앞에 절(you’ll ~  balance)을 선행사로 부연 설명하는 관계사절의 동사 자리로, 절 전체가 선행사일 때 단수 취급하므로 단수도 수일치한 단수동사 is는 적 절하다. 18) ④: (A) 신체는 균형을 유지할 필요가 있는 에너지 장부책 과 같다고 했고, 섭취하는 모든 음식이 장부 속 수입이 라고 했으므로 균형을 유지하기 위해 에너지를 ‘소비 해’야 한다는 흐름이 자연스럽다. 따라서 빈칸에 들어 갈 말로 적절한 것은 expend(소비하다), consume(소모 하다), spend(소비하다)이다. (B) 앞에서 과잉 에너지를 사용하지 않고 너무 많은 음 식을 섭취하면 신체는 그 추가분을 지방으로 저장하게 된다고 했으므로 이것이 ‘건강에 좋지’ 않다는 흐름이 자연스럽다. 따라서 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 적절한 것은 sound(건강한), healthy(건강한), good(좋은)이다. 오답 ① 아끼다 건강한 ② 소비하다 건강하지 못한 ③ 소모하다 해로운 ⑤ 보존하다 좋은

위 대화의 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 알맞게 연결된 것은?

(A)                      (B)
choices: SoIn short
HoweverIn brief
ThereforeTo illustrate this point
NonethelessTo give you an example
For exampleOn the contrary
solution: (A) 자신은 컴퓨터 게임에 관심이 있고 상당히 창의적이라는 앞 내용을 이유로 컴퓨터 게임 회사를 시작하는 것을 고려중 이라는 결론을 연결하므로, 빈칸에는 So(그래서)나 Therefore (그러므로, 따라서)가 적절하다. (B) 다양한 과목을 공부함으로써 영감을 얻을 수 있다는 앞 내 용에 대한 구체적 예시로 많은 컴퓨터 업계 최고 경영자들은 자신들이 수강했던 철학, 심리학, 또는 역사학 과정이 다양한 방식으로 그들에게 영감을 주었다고 말한다는 내용을 연결하 고 있으므로, 빈칸에는 To illustrate this point(이 요점을 예를 들어 설명하자면) 또는 To give you an example(예시를 하나 들자면)이 적절하다.

body:
Hello,
everyone!
Thank
you
for
your
warm
welcome. (A)고향 같은 곳에 돌아와서 좋지만 오늘은
공연을 하러가 아니라 뮤지션으로서의 제 삶에 대해
이야기하려고 여러분을 방문했습니다. Last year, after
20 years of hard work, I finally signed my first
record company contract. I’d like to tell you a
hopeful story and ⓐgive some insight into the hard
work that I had to put in.
Look at this picture of Picasso’s The Old Guitarist
behind me. My grandfather was a classical guitarist,
and on my 13th birthday, he gave me this picture
and a new guitar. After he passed away, I hung it
up in my room as a reminder of his love for music.
I wasn’t a musical genius, but I was better than
most. I was popular at school festivals, and I
thought I was born to be a musician. But things
were far from easy. In college, I had to compete
with classmates who were definitely more capable
than I was. I don’t even remember how many
contests I went to and came up short. I kept failing
ⓑno matter how hard I tried. It seemed like every
disappointment made me lose hope more and
more. I wanted to give up.
The funny thing was ⓒwhenever anyone asked me
to play a song for them, I would be so happy.
Although my dream was to record an album, the
reality was I probably wouldn’t make it. Then one
day, I looked at the picture of The Old Guitarist on
my
wall.
I
suddenly
remembered
what
my
grandfather had told me about Picasso: only a tiny
fraction of the thousands of artworks he created
during his lifetime are recognized by the public.
Then I thought of my grandfather and how he
loved playing, ⓓpracticing his art his entire life,
even without fame. I realized the only way to
become an old guitarist like him was ⓔto keep
playing.

윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ를 아래와 같이 전환할 때, 알맞지 않은 것은?
choices: ⓐ: give → to give
ⓑ: no matter how hard → however hard
ⓒ: whenever → every time
ⓓ: practicing → to practice
ⓔ: to keep → keeping
solution: ⓓ 앞의 완전한 절(he loved playing)에 콤마(,)로 연결된 ‘practicing his art his entire life’는 흐름상 부대상황(~하면서) 을 나타내는 분사구문이므로, 현재분사 practicing을 to부정사 인 to practice로는 바꿀 수 없다. 참고로, 분사구문은 흐름상 적절한 접속사를 사용해 ‘접속사+주어+동사~’의 부사절로 바 꾸어 쓸 수 있으므로 while/as he practiced[was practicing]와 같이 전환할 수 있다.

The second point I want to make today ⓐto be
about thinking that your personality is fixed. Many
people believe that their personality falls into a
specific
category
and
often
ⓑblaming
their
weaknesses or failures on their personality type. For
example, they may say ⓒwhat they can’t do
something because they aren’t that kind of person.
However, personality categorizations are neither
absolute nor permanent.
Try to remember ourselves from ten years ago.
Who was your favorite singer? What did you hope
to become when you grow up? Do you feel the
same way now? What will your answers be 10 years
from now? I bet you don’t know. Just like your
likes and future dreams keep changing, so do you.
If you choose ⓓbehaving differently and make
needed changes, your personality will also change.

Hello, my name is Laura Thompson, and I’m a
guidance counselor at the local college. I also have
a social media channel where I give advice to
young students like you. Today I’d like to talk to
you about two things that I hope will inspire you.
Let me start by asking you a question. Have you
ever asked yourself whether you made a good
impression on someone you just met? In fact, most
people believe they make a worse impression than
they actually do. Researchers performed an experiment
where students were paired up for five-minute ice
breaking conversations. They were then asked to rate
how much they liked their partners. Additionally,
researchers asked participants if they thought their
partners liked them. Most participants’ estimations
of their partners’ responses were pessimistic, which
were opposite to the real responses. It turns out
that participants (A)___________________________________.
The researchers coined a new term, the “liking
gap,” for this difference in perception or the
mismatch between how we perceive ourselves and
what others actually think of us. How is this helpful
for you? We often underestimate ourselves based
on our assumption of how others might judge us.
In other words, our fixed attitudes may prevent us
from reaching our true potential. Don’t worry about
the impression you think you make on people;
chances
are
you
can
be
confident
that
the
impression you make is just fine.

do not care about whether their partners likethem or not

Then, what do people do with the remaining 400
calories? They may be burned by intense physical
exercise like jogging, working out at the gym, playing
badminton or tennis, or venturing out for a hike.
However, those calories may also be burned by small,
seemingly unimportant activities we do throughout
the day, like standing up and sitting down, walking
around the house, washing dishes, doing the laundry,
taking out the garbage, and many others. These
actions are collectively called Non-Exercise Activity
Thermogenesis (NEAT) as they use up energy too!
For example, a 40-minute run will burn around 400
calories. (A)[Do / Doing] this could use up the excess
energy budget completely, but not everyone has 40
minutes a day to go for a run. Taking 10,000 steps,
which (B)[is / are] like walking about 8 kilometers,
burns 400 calories as well. What this means is that
while a 40-minute run will burn 400 calories, doing
small things like more walking, taking stairs, or even
just (C)[clean / cleaning] your room can add up at
the end of the day, too.
Each gram of body fat contains about 9 calories, so
if you spend your day eating and not moving, your
body may convert the 400 calories into 44 grams of
fat. This is not healthy over the long term. While
NEAT doesn’t provide the heart and muscles with
the same benefits that exercise does, excess energy
still gets used up instead of being stored. You may
not necessarily get fit, but you’ll stay in energy
balance, which is important for long term health.

through intense exercise but also through

walking around the house. (T/F)

consume energy even though they are not
formal exercise. (T/F)

run can effectively deplete their daily excess
energy budget of 400 calories. (T/F)

energy may be stored in the body as fat. (T/F)

body:
Then, what do people do with the remaining 400
calories? They may be burned by intense physical
exercise like jogging, working out at the gym, playing
badminton or tennis, or venturing out for a hike.
However, those calories may also be burned by small,
seemingly unimportant activities we do throughout
the day, like standing up and sitting down, walking
around the house, washing dishes, doing the laundry,
taking out the garbage, and many others. These
actions are collectively called Non-Exercise Activity
Thermogenesis (NEAT) as they use up energy too!
For example, a 40-minute run will burn around 400
calories. (A)[Do / Doing] this could use up the excess
energy budget completely, but not everyone has 40
minutes a day to go for a run. Taking 10,000 steps,
which (B)[is / are] like walking about 8 kilometers,
burns 400 calories as well. What this means is that
while a 40-minute run will burn 400 calories, doing
small things like more walking, taking stairs, or even
just (C)[clean / cleaning] your room can add up at
the end of the day, too.
Each gram of body fat contains about 9 calories, so
if you spend your day eating and not moving, your
body may convert the 400 calories into 44 grams of
fat. This is not healthy over the long term. While
NEAT doesn’t provide the heart and muscles with
the same benefits that exercise does, excess energy
still gets used up instead of being stored. You may
not necessarily get fit, but you’ll stay in energy
balance, which is important for long term health.

간 동안 더 활동적으로 지내려고 하는 것이든, NEAT
을 이해하는 것은 몸의 에너지 균형을 유지하는 훌륭
한 방법이다.
In the big picture, your body is like an energy
account book that ⓓneeds to be balanced. All the
food you eat is credit in the account, and you
need to spend energy to keep it all in balance.
Thus if you eat too much food without using the
excess energy, your body will store the extra as fat,
ⓔwhat is not healthy. Remember, standing uses
more energy than sitting, walking uses more energy
than standing, and running uses more energy than
walking, so let’s all keep moving, stay active, and
use our energy wisely for a healthier life!

body:
The answer to this requires a simple formula and
a little bit of math. The formula is an easy
equation: the total energy expenditure of the body
equals 「BMR + TEF + PA」. In the human body, the
energy from different foods people eat is used to
keep
everything
running
smoothly.
The
basal
metabolic rate (BMR) is a measurement of how
much energy is needed to stay alive; the thermic
effect of food (TEF) is a measurement of the energy
used to consume and absorb energy from food;
and physical activity (PA) is a measurement of the
energy _______________________________________. Learning
about the composition of these three elements can
help people make better choices for their health
and well-being.
Most of the energy the body uses each day is set
or fixed. Assuming an energy input of 2,000
calories, about 1,400 calories, or 70%, goes to
essential functions such as keeping the heart and
the brain working; this is called the basal metabolic
rate (BMR). Around 200 calories, or 10%, is used to
consume and absorb energy from food and is
called the thermic effect of food (TEF). In short,
BMR and TEF are the minimum energy required for
the body to stay alive. The remaining 400 calories,
or 20%, is used for things people choose to do,
including various physical activities (PA) like working,
playing, and moving around. Maybe some of the
London public transportation workers spent the
remaining 20% differently, resulting in their different
health outcomes.

윗글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?
choices: used solely for high-intensity sports or structuredexercise
utilized in breaking down and absorbing foodnutrients
necessary to support vital functions while thebody is at rest
produced by the brain to regulate heartbeatand body functions
expended in physical activities beyond basiclife-sustaining needs
solution: 정답은 ⑤ 이다. (해설 없음)

The second point I want to make today is about
thinking that your personality is fixed. Many people
believe that their personality falls into a specific
category and often (A)[blame / blames] their
weaknesses or failures on their personality type. For
example, they may say they can’t do something
because they aren’t that kind of person. However,
personality categorizations are neither absolute nor
(B)[permanent / permanently].
Try to remember yourself from ten years ago.
Who was your favorite singer? What did you hope
to become when you grow up? Do you feel the
same way now? What will your answers be 10 years
from now? I bet you don’t know. Just like your
likes and future dreams keep changing, so (C)[do /
are] you. If you choose to behave differently and
make needed changes, your personality will also
change. People are predictable and consistent over
time only because they choose to be, so don’t limit
yourself to a certain type. Start crafting the person
you want to become today.

(B)
(C)

Hello, my name is Laura Thompson, and I’m a
guidance counselor at the local college. I also have
a social media channel where I give advice to
young students like you. Today I’d like to talk to
you about two things that I hope will inspire you.
Let me start by asking you a question. Have you
ever asked yourself whether you made a good
impression on someone you just met? In fact, most
people believe they make a (A)[better / worse]
impression
than
they
actually
do.
Researchers
performed an experiment where students were
paired up for five-minute ice breaking conversations.
They were then asked to rate how much they liked
their
partners.
Additionally,
researchers
asked
participants if they thought their partners liked
them.
Most
participants’
estimations
of
their
partners’ responses were (B)[optimistic / pessimistic],
which were opposite to the real responses. It turns
out that participants do not make bad impressions
but make better impressions than they think.
The researchers coined a new term, the “liking
gap,” for this difference in perception or the
mismatch between how we perceive ourselves and
what others actually think of us. How is this helpful
for you? We often (C)[overestimate / underestimate]
ourselves based on our assumption of how others
might judge us. In other words, our fixed attitudes
may prevent us from reaching our true potential.
Don’t worry about the impression you think you
make on people; chances are you can be confident
that the impression you make is just fine.

(B) 뒤에 실제의 반응과는 정반대였으며, 참가자들은 나쁜 인 상을 주지 않고 그들이 생각하는 것보다 더 좋은 인상을 주는 것으로 드러났다는 내용이 이어지므로, 참가자들의 자신들의 파트너에 대한 평가는 비관적이었다는 흐름으로 pessimistic(비 관적인)이 적절하다. (C) 뒤에 In other words(다시 말해)로 연결되는 문장에서 우 리의 고정된 태도는 우리가 진정한 잠재력에 도달하는 것을 막을 수 있다고 환언하고 있으므로, 우리 자신이 나쁜 인상을 준다고 생각하는 우리의 고정된 태도로서, 우리가 흔히 다른 사람들이 우리를 어떻게 판단할지에 대한 추정에 근거해 우리 자신을 과소평가한다는 흐름으로 underestimate(~을 과소평가 하다)가 적절하다.

body:
London Transport Workers Study
In the busy London streets of 1953, a special
study was conducted. Scientists observed more than
31,000 people ⓐwhich had various jobs on buses
and trains. Some jobs demanded lots of moving
around, like ticket collectors, while others, like
drivers, didn’t require much movement. What was
interesting ⓑwere that the workers with more active
jobs had fewer heart problems than those who sat
a lot. This implied that jobs requiring more moving
around were healthier for workers than those jobs
that ⓒwasn’t. That could account for the difference
in their health outcomes?
Most of the energy the body ⓓis used each day
is set or fixed. Assuming an energy input of 2,000
calories, about 1,400 calories, or 70%, goes to
essential functions such as keeping the heart and
the brain working; this is called the basal metabolic
rate (BMR). Around 200 calories, or 10%, is used to
consume and absorb energy from food and is
called the thermic effect of food (TEF). In short,
(A)BMR과 TEF는 신체가 생명을 유지하는 데 필요한
최소한의 에너지이다. The remaining 400 calories, or
20%, is used for things people choose to do,
including various physical activities (PA) like working,
playing, and ⓔmove around. Maybe some of the
London public transportation workers spent the
remaining 20% differently, resulting in their different
health outcomes.

body:
Each gram of body fat contains about 9 calories, so if
you spend your day (A)[to eat / eating] and not moving,
your body may convert the 400 calories into 44 grams of
fat. This is not healthy over the long term. While NEAT
doesn’t provide the heart and muscles with the same
benefits (B)[what / that] exercise does, excess energy still
gets used up instead of being stored. You may not
necessarily get fit, but you’ll stay in energy balance,
(C)[which / that] is important for long term health.
Paying attention to NEAT has other health benefits
as well. Sitting too much can cause problems like
heart disease and muscle loss, so standing not only
increases NEAT but also decreases sitting time,
which is a win-win. As people get older, it may
become more difficult to stay healthy, so adopting a
lifestyle that maximizes NEAT is a good habit for
younger people to make. Walking more, taking
stairs, or even using smaller water cups so they
have to be refilled more often uses energy. Whether
it’s for weight management or trying to stay more
active during exam week, understanding NEAT is a
great way to maintain energy balance in the body.

stay active, and use our energy wisely for a
healthier life!

Then, what do people do with the remaining 400
calories? They may be burned by intense physical
exercise like jogging, working out at the gym,
playing badminton or tennis, or venturing out for a
hike. (A) However, those calories may also be
burned by small, seemingly unimportant activities
we do throughout the day, like standing up and
sitting down, walking around the house, washing
dishes, doing the laundry, taking out the garbage,
and many others. (B) For example, a 40-minute run
will burn around 400 calories. (C) Doing this could
use up the excess energy budget completely, but
not everyone has 40 minutes a day to go for a
run. (D) Taking 10,000 steps, which is like walking
about 8 kilometers, burns 400 calories as well. (E)
What this means is that while a 40-minute run will
burn 400 calories, doing small things like more
walking, taking stairs, or even just cleaning your
room can add up at the end of the day, too.

Paying attention to NEAT has other health benefits
as well. Sitting too much can cause problems like
heart disease and muscle loss, so standing not only
increases NEAT but also decreases sitting time,
which is a win-win. As people get older, it may
become more difficult to stay healthy, so adopting
a lifestyle that maximizes NEAT is a good habit for
younger people to make. Walking more, taking
stairs, or even using smaller water cups so they
have to be refilled more often uses energy.
Whether it’s for weight management or trying to
stay more active during exam week, understanding
NEAT is a great way to maintain energy balance in
the body.

(B) ‘음식을 섭취하고 에너지를 흡수하는 데 사용되는’을 뜻하므로 to consume과 등위접속사 and로 병렬 연결되 어야 한다. 따라서 to consume의 to를 생략한 동사원형 absorb가 적절하다. (C) 사역동사 help, 목적어 people에 이어지는 목적격보 어 자리이므로 동사원형 make가 적절하다. 5) The Equation for Total Energy Expenditure and Its Three Key Factors 제시문 신체의 총에너지 소비량을 위한 방정식과 그것의 세 가지 핵심 요소들 6) Taking 10,000 steps, which is like walking about, burns 400 calories : • take 10,000 steps를 동명사로 변형하여 주어 Taking 10,000 steps를 작성한다. • ‘약 8킬로미터를 걷는 것과 같은 10,000보를 걷는 것’을 영작하기 위해 Taking 10,000 steps 뒤에 콤마(,)와 계속 적 용법의 관계대명사 which를 차례대로 쓰고, 선행사 Taking 10,000 steps는 단수이므로 which 뒤에 단수동사 is를 이어 쓴다. • ‘~와 같은’을 뜻하는 전치사 like와 전치사의 목적어로 동명사 walking을 쓴 뒤, 거리를 나타내는 8 kilometers 앞에 ‘약’의 의미를 갖는 about을 쓴다. • 주어 Taking 10,000 steps는 단수이므로 관계사절 뒤에 콤마(,)와 단수동사 burns를 쓰고 목적어 400 calories를 이어 쓴다. 7) ④: ⓓ required → requiring (명사절 접속사 that이 이끄는 절에서 동사 were가 뒤에 있으므로 주어 jobs를 수식하 는 분사 자리이며, jobs가 더 많은 움직임을 ‘필요로 하 영어1 비상(홍민표) S.U1 예상문제 2회 - 주관식(서답형) 2. BMR and TEF are the minimum energy required for the body to stay alive 5. The Equation for Total Energy Expenditure and Its Three Key Factors 6. Taking 10,000 steps, which is like walking about, burns 400 calories 는’ 주체이므로 required를 능동의 의미인 현재분사 requiring으로 고친다.) 오답 ⓐ 주어 a special study가 ‘진행된’ 대상이므로 be동사 was와 함께 쓰여 수동태(be+p.p.)를 이루는 과거분사 conducted는 적절하다. ⓑ 주어가 없는 불완전한 절(was interesting)을 이끌어 선행사 없이 주어 역할을 하는 명사절을 이루고 있으므 로 선행사를 포함하는 관계대명사 What은 적절하다. ⓒ 주어가 없는 불완전한 절(sat a lot)을 이끌어 workers를 가리키는 선행사 those를 수식하는 관계사절 을 이루고 있으므로, 선행사가 사람일 때 쓰는 주격 관 계대명사 who는 적절하다. ⓔ 주어가 없는 불완전한 절(didn't)을 이끌어 선행사 those jobs를 수식하는 관계사절을 이루고 있으므로 주 격 관계대명사 that은 적절하다. 참고로 didn't은 didn't require moving around를 의미한다. 8) ④: (A) 뒤에서 활동량이 많은 직업과 적은 직업을 비교하고 있으므로 흐름상 ‘다양한’ 직업들이 자연스럽다. 따라서 various(다양한)가 적절하다. same 동일한 (B) 뒤에서 더 많이 움직이는 직업이 그렇지 않은 직업 보다 근로자의 건강에 더 좋다는 것을 암시했다고 했으 므로 흐름상 활동량이 많은 노동자들이 심장 질환이 ‘더 적었다’는 것이 자연스럽다. 따라서 ‘fewer(더 적은)’가 적 절하다. more 더 많은 (C) 더 많이 움직이는 직업이 그렇지 않은 직업보다 근 로자의 건강에 더 좋다고 했으므로 그들의 건강 결과에 ‘차이’가 있다는 흐름이 자연스럽다. 따라서 difference(차 이)가 적절하다. similarity 유사점 9) ②: (A) 동사 spend는 ‘spend+목적어+~ing(~하는 데 …를 보내다)’의 구조를 취해야 하며, 등위접속사 and 뒤에 not moving과도 병렬로 연결되어야 하므로 목적어 your day 뒤에 eating이 이어지는 것이 적절하다. (B) 목적어가 없는 불완전한 절(exercise does)을 이끌어 선행사 the same benefits를 수식하는 관계사절을 이루 어야 하므로 목적격 관계대명사 that이 적절하다. (C) 주어가 없는 불완전한 절(is ~ health)을 이끌어 앞 절 전체를 부연 설명하는 관계사절을 이루어야 하므로 계속적 용법의 관계대명사 which가 적절하다. 10) ⑤: 일상에서 걷기, 서 있기, 계단 이용하기와 같은 작은 움 직임(NEAT)을 늘리면 과잉 에너지가 지방으로 저장되 는 것을 막아 에너지 균형을 유지할 수 있으며, 이는 장기적으로 체중 관리와 장기적으로 전반적인 건강 유 지에 중요한 역할을 한다는 것의 핵심 내용이므로 이 글의 주제로 적절한 것은 ⑤ ‘에너지 균형과 건강을 유 지하도록 돕는 NEAT‘이다. 오답 ① 신체적 요구 측면에서 일상의 가벼운 활동과 고강도 운동의 동등함 ② NEAT가 근력 강화와 심장 건강에 미치는 긍정적인 영향 ③ 섭취량보다 에너지 소비를 극대화함으로써 체중을 줄이기 위한 간단한 공식 ④ 젊은 사람들이 NEAT를 통해 운동 수행 능력을 성취 하기 위한 전략들 11) ③: (A) 뒤에서 심장과 뇌를 작동시키는 것과 같은 기능들 이라고 했으므로 ‘필수적인’ 기능들이라는 흐름이 자연 스럽다. 따라서 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 적절한 것은 fundamental(근본적인), essential(필수적인), vital(생명 유지에 필수적인)이다. (B) 뒤에서 일, 놀이, 이동과 같은 다양한 신체 활동들 이 언급됐으므로 사람들이 하기로 ‘선택한’ 활동들이라 는 흐름이 자연스럽다. 따라서 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 적 절한 것은 opt(선택하다), choose(선택하다), decide(결 정하다)이다. 오답 ① 근본적인 주저하다 ② 불필요한 선택하다 ④ 생명 유지에 필수적인 필요로 하다 ⑤ 부차적인 결정하다 12) ⑤: 런던 대중교통 근로자 중 일부가 남은 20%의 에너지를 다르게 소비하여 다른 건강 결과를 얻었을 것이라는 것만 추정했을 뿐, 구체적으로 어떤 질병과 관련이 있 는지는 언급되지 않았으므로 ⑤ ‘런던 대중교통 근로자 들의 서로 다른 건강 결과와 관련된 특정 질병들은 무 엇인가?‘는 답할 수 없는 질문이다. 오답 ① 인간 신체의 총에너지 소비량을 계산하는 데 사용 되는 수학적 공식은 무엇인가? (→신체의 총에너지 소 비량 = BMR+TEF+PA) ② 어떤 요소들이 인간 신체가 생명을 유지하기 위해 필요한 최소한의 에너지를 구성하는가? (→기초 대사율 (BMR)과 식이성 발열 효과(TEF)) ③ 음식을 섭취하고 영양분을 흡수하는 과정 동안 소 비되는 에너지를 가리키는 용어는 무엇인가? (→식이성 발열 효과(TEF)) ④ 하루 섭취량을 2,000칼로리로 가정할 때, 얼마나 많 은 에너지가 식이성 발열 효과(TEF)에 구체적으로 할당 되는가? (→약 200칼로리) 13) ①: 우리의 신체를 균형을 유지해야 하는 에너지 장부책으 로 비유하여, 음식을 섭취하면 균형을 유지하기 위해 에너지를 소비해야 한다고 했으므로 과잉 에너지를 사 용하지 않고 너무 많은 음식을 섭취하면 살이 찌고, 이 는 건강에 좋지 않다는 흐름이 자연스럽다. 따라서 빈 칸에 들어갈 말로 적절한 것은 ① ‘남는 에너지를 체지 방으로 저장하다’이다. 오답 ② 모든 영양소를 신체적인 힘(체력)으로 전환하다 ③ 자동으로 총칼로리 섭취량을 줄이다 ④ 여러 장기를 통해 남은 칼로리를 방출하다 ⑤ 장부 균형을 유지하기 위해 더 많은 음식을 요구하다 14) ②: 주어진 문장은 ‘이러한 행동 또한 에너지를 소모하기 때문에 비운동성 활동 열 생성(NEAT)이라고 통칭한다.’ 라는 의미이다. 따라서 이 문장 앞에는 ‘These actions‘로 지칭될 운동이 아닌 일상적인 활동들이 먼저 제시되어 야 한다. 따라서 ‘일어서고 앉기, 집 안에서 돌아다니 기, 설거지하기, 빨래하기, 쓰레기 내다 버리기 등’과 같은 운동이 아닌 일상적인 활동들이 구체적으로 제시 되어 있는 문장 뒤이자, 주어진 문장에 언급된 내용(에 너지 소모)에 대한 구체적인 수치로 강렬한 운동 못지 않게 NEAT가 에너지를 소비한다는 예를 들고 있는 문 장 앞인 (B)에 들어가는 것이 알맞다. 15) ⑤: 앞에서 우리가 하루 종일 하는 작고 사소해 보이는 활 동에 의해서도 칼로리가 소모되며 40분 달리기와 마찬 가지로 더 많이 걷거나 계단을 이용하거나 방을 청소 하는 등의 작은 활동도 하루가 끝날 때 합산될 수 있 다고 했으므로 ⑤ ‘사소한 집안일들은 너무 미미해서 하루가 끝날 때 사용되는 총 에너지 양에 기여하지 못 한다.’는 일치하지 않는 내용이다. 오답 ① 심지어 우리가 단순히 서 있거나 앉아 있을 때에도, 신체는 에너지를 필요로 한다. ② NEAT는 체계적인 운동보다는 사소한 일상적 움직임 을 통해 소모되는 에너지를 일컫는다. ③ 약 10,000보를 걷는 것은 총 칼로리 소모 측면에서 40분간의 달리기와 대략적으로 맞먹는다. ④ 신체적 제약이나 일정은 모든 사람들이 매일 40분 의 조깅에 전념하는 것을 막을 수 있다. 16) ⑤: (E) saves(절약하다) → uses(사용하다) 17) ⑤: ‘그렇다면 사람들은 남은 400칼로리를 어떻게 사용할까? ‘라는 주어진 글 뒤에 the remaining 400 calories를 They로 이어받아 질문에 대한 답변으로 격렬한 신체 운동과 작고 사소한 활동들에 의해 남은 칼로리가 소모 될 수 있다고 설명하는 (C), (C)의 마지막 문장에서 언 급된 작고 사소한 활동들을 These actions(이러한 행동 들)로 이어받아 이러한 행동들이 비운동성 활동 열 생 성(NEAT)이라고 불린다고 설명하는 (B), (B)의 마지막 문장에서는 NEAT 역시 에너지를 소모한다는 점을 강조 하기 위해 For example(예를 들어)을 사용하여 ‘40분 달리기는 400칼로리를 소모한다’라는 구체적인 수치를 제시한 뒤, ‘40분 달리기’를 Doing this로 이어받아 그 러한 운동이 남은 에너지를 모두 소모할 수 있음을 설 명하고, 이어서 10,000보 걷기 역시 같은 양의 칼로리 를 소모할 수 있다는 추가 예시를 제시하는 (A)로 이어 지는 흐름이 자연스럽다. 18) ⑤: NEAT를 늘리는 생활 습관은 단순히 앉아 있는 시간을 줄이는 것뿐만 아니라, 걷기, 계단 오르기, 작은 활동들 처럼 일상 속 움직임을 통해 추가 에너지를 소모하게 해 주며, 이를 통해 건강 유지, 체중 관리, 에너지 균형 유지 등 다양한 장기적인 건강상의 이점을 제공한다고 했으므로 이 글의 주제로 적절한 것은 ⑤ ‘NEAT에 주 의를 기울이는 것이 필요한 이유’이다. 오답 ① 체계적인 운동이 건강을 개선시키는 데 있어서 일 상의 생활 방식 변화보다 더 나은 성과를 내는 이유 ② 신체 건강에 미치는 사소한 신체 활동들의 미미한 영향 ③ 자신의 활동 수준에 기반한 에너지 균형을 달성하는 방법 ④ 장수를 위해 좌식 습관을 없애야 할 필요성

Hello, my name is Laura Thompson, and I’m a
guidance counselor at the local college. I also have
a social media channel where I give advice to
young students like you. Today I’d like to talk to
you about two things that I hope will inspire you.
Let me start by asking you a question. Have you
ever asked yourself whether you made a good
impression on someone you just met? (A)___________,
most people believe they make a worse impression
than they actually do. Researchers performed an
experiment where students were paired up for
five-minute ice breaking conversations. They were
then asked to rate how much they liked their
partners. (B)___________, researchers asked participants
if they thought their partners liked them. Most
participants’ estimations of their partners’ responses
were pessimistic, which were opposite to the real
responses. It turns out that participants do not
make bad impressions but make better impressions
than they think.
The researchers coined a new term, the “liking
gap,” for this difference in perception or the
mismatch between how we perceive ourselves and
what others actually think of us. How is this helpful
for you? We often underestimate ourselves based
on our assumption of how others might judge us.
(C)___________, our fixed attitudes may prevent us
from reaching our true potential. Don’t worry about
the impression you think you make on people;
chances
are
you
can
be
confident
that
the
impression you make is just fine.

윗글의 빈칸 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 알맞게 연결된 것은?

(A)
(B)
(C)
choices: In factHoweverIn contrast
In factAdditionallyIn other words
For exampleLikewiseIn contrast
ActuallyHoweverIn conclusion
For exampleAdditionallyIn other words
solution: (A) 방금 만난 사람에게 좋은 인상을 주었는지 스스로에게 물 어본 적이 있는가에 관한 질문에 대해 대부분의 사람들은 자 신이 실제로 주는 것보다 더 나쁜 인상을 준다고 믿는다는 사 실을 제시하고 있으므로, 빈칸에는 예상과 다르거나 놀랄만한 사실을 덧붙일 때 사용하는 In fact(사실은)나 actually(실제로 는, 사실은)가 적절하다. (B) 실험 참가자들은 자신들의 파트너가 얼마나 마음에 들었는 지 평가하도록 요청받았다는 내용 뒤에 파트너가 자신을 좋아 한다고 생각하는지 물었다는 추가적인 요청에 대해 언급하고 있으므로, 빈칸에는 Additionally(추가로, 게다가)가 적절하다. (C) 우리는 흔히 다른 사람이 우리를 어떻게 판단할지에 대한 추정에 근거하여 우리 자신을 과소평가한다는 앞의 내용에 대 해, 우리의 고정된 태도는 우리가 진정한 잠재력에 도달하는 것을 막을 수 있다는 말로 바꿔 앞 내용의 요점을 다시 짚어 말하고 있으므로, 빈칸에는 In other words(바꿔 말하면, 즉)가 적절하다.

body:
The second point I want to make today is about
thinking that your personality is fixed. Many people
believe that their personality falls into a specific
category and often blame their weaknesses or
failures on their personality type. For example, they
may say they can’t do something because they
aren’t that kind of person. However, personality
categorizations are neither absolute nor permanent.
Try to remember yourself from ten years ago.
Who was your favorite singer? What did you hope
to become when you grow up? Do you feel the
same way now? What will your answers be 10 years
from now? I bet you don’t know. Just like your
likes and future dreams keep changing, so do you.
If you (A)_______________________________________________
____________________, your personality will also change.
People are predictable and consistent over time
only because they choose to be, so don’t limit
yourself to a certain type. Start crafting the person
you want to become today.

윗글의 빈칸 (A)에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?
choices: focus on past failures rather than future goals
avoid challenges that conflict with your personality
assume your future self will be the same as youare now
choose to behave differently and make neededchanges
try to find hobbies and jobs that suit yournatural personality
solution: 많은 사람들이 자신의 성격이 고정되어 있다고 잘못 생각하지 만 성격 분류는 절대적이지도 영구적이지도 않으며, 사람은 오 직 자신이 그렇게 하기로 선택했기 때문에 시간이 지나도 예 측 가능하고 변하지 않는 것이므로 특정 유형으로 자신을 제 한하지 말고 오늘부터 자신이 되고 싶은 사람을 만들기를 시 작하라고 했으므로, 변화를 만들기 위해 노력할 때 원하는 방 향으로 성격이 바뀔 수 있다는 흐름이 되어야 한다. 따라서 빈 칸에는 ❹ ‘다른 방식으로 행동하고 필요한 변화를 만들기로 선택한다’가 적절하다.

body:
The funny thing was whenever anyone asked me
to play a song for them, I would be so happy.
Although my dream was to record an album, the
reality was I probably wouldn’t (A)[succeed / fail].
Then one day, I looked at the picture of The Old
Guitarist on my wall. I suddenly remembered what
my grandfather had told me about Picasso: only a
tiny fraction of the thousands of artworks he
created during his lifetime are recognized by the
public. Then I thought of my grandfather and how
he loved playing, practicing his art his entire life,
even without fame. I realized the only way to
become an old guitarist like him was to keep
playing.
The happy ending to this story is that after having
sent my recordings to countless producers, I finally
found one who was eager to work with me. One
thing led to another, and I finally (B)[signed / gave
up] a record deal. Opportunities only come to
those
who are
prepared. I
had
spent
years
performing on (C)[famous / unknown] streets and
writing songs no one recognized. The difficulties I
faced were part of my journey. If you love
something, keep trying. Someday an opportunity
may come knocking at your door, and you have to
be ready to welcome it.

solution: (A) 음반을 녹음하는 것이 꿈이었지만 현실은 아마 성공하지 못할 것 같았다는 대조적인 흐름으로 wouldn’t 뒤에 succeed (성공하다)가 적절하다. (B) 마침내 자신과 함께 작업하기를 몹시 원하는 프로듀서를 찾았고, 하나의 일이 다른 일로 이어졌다는 내용 뒤에 마침내 음반 계약을 체결했다는 최종적인 결과가 이어지는 흐름으로, signed(서명했다)가 적절하다. (C) 자신에게 마침내 기회가 오기까지 겪었던 어려움들을 언급 하는 맥락이므로, 무명의 거리에서 공연하고 아무도 알아주지 않는 곡을 쓰며 여러 해를 보냈다는 흐름으로 unknown(알려 지지 않은)이 적절하다.

I wasn’t a musical genius, but I was better than
most. I was popular at school festivals, and I
thought I was born to be a musician. But things
were far from easy. In college, I had to compete
with classmates who were definitely more capable
than I was. I don’t even remember how many
contests I went to and came up short. I kept failing
no matter how hard I tried. It seemed like every
disappointment made me lose hope more and
more. I wanted to give up.

다음 글의 제목으로 알맞은 것은?

During New York Fashion Week 2018, a woman
with a brightly decorated prosthetic leg proudly
walked the runway at a major fashion show. She
was Mama Cax, a model and influencer.
Cax was diagnosed with cancer at age 14 and lost
her right leg at 16 after surgery. At first, Cax was
depressed and struggled to accept her new body.
However, with the support of her family and
friends, Cax learned to love it. One day when she
was 26, Cax posted a picture on social media
showing her leg. “I didn’t think it could help
anyone,” she said in an interview, “But after receiving
messages of support, I realized my story could
inspire others.” After receiving support from others,
she began to use social media to share more about
her life and to inspire others. She proudly posted
pictures of herself wearing stylish prosthetic covers
and spoke out about body positivity and fashion. In
2016,
she
became
the
first
model
for
the
#RunwayForAll campaign. In 2018, she appeared on
the cover of major fashion magazines.
When asked, “How did you come to embrace
yourself?” she replied, “The truth is, like many
people, I’m still on my journey to self-love. There
are many barriers ahead.” In addition to modeling,
Cax showed her ability to overcome physical
barriers
by
swimming,
playing
basketball,
and
mountain climbing. She even finished the New York
City Marathon in a wheelchair.
Sadly, Mama Cax’s journey was cut short in 2019.
Although she is no longer with us, her journey will
remain in our hearts, inspiring us to overcome
limitations and find our own paths to success and
happiness.

W: This picture of Chand Baori is stunning! I can’t
wait to go this summer.
M: It’s even more amazing in person. (A)Is it okay if
I tell you something about Indian culture?
W: Of course.
M: Well, feet are thought to be the dirtiest part of
the body in India, so it’s considered disrespectful
to touch books with your feet.
W: Disrespectful to books?
M: Yes, because books represent knowledge to
Indians. Touching them with your feet is like
touching another person with your feet.
W: But what if I accidentally touch a book with my
feet?
M: In that case, you should hold the book and
touch it to your forehead as a sign of apology.
W: Thanks for the information!
M: No problem! I hope you have a wonderful time
in India!

“Good things come in small packages,” they say.
Indeed, some cultures around the world appreciate
the importance of small things, often ⓐput them
together to create amazing works of art. Often,
practical need or creative desire plays a key role in
such efforts.
Stitched Together
(A)패치워크는 그것의 아름다움이 세계의 많은 문화
권에서 오래도록 인정받아 왔으며, 천 조각들을 꿰매
어 더 큰 예술품으로 창조하는 것을 수반하는 바느질
의 한 종류이다. ⓑEvery culture is proud of its own
patterns, including Koreans, who take pride in their
unique style, jogakbo. ⓒCreating during the Joseon
dynasty, it is a type of traditional wrapping cloth
ⓓmade by stitching small pieces of fabric into a
large square or rectangle. Frugal women did not
want to waste any fabric and found ways ⓔto
reuse it. However, jogakbo was ⓕmuch more than
just repurposing fabric. It often told the creator’s
life story because a finished piece contained fabric
scraps from her wedding skirt, her husband’s shirt,
and her children’s clothes. The practical need to
repurpose leftover patches gave birth to a novel art
form.

Strung Together
Throughout the ages and across all cultures, there
have been small decorative objects with a hole for
threading
ⓐcall
beads.
In
its
simplest
form,
beadwork can involve threading a few beads
together on a single string ⓑto make a simple
bracelet or necklace, or on a larger scale, to form
beaded bags, clothing, or even wall-hangings. (A)구
슬 공예는 아주 오래된 것으로, 석기 시대까지 거슬러
올라가는 구슬들의 발견에 의해 입증되었다. Back
then, people strung bones, shells, or rocks together
to hang around their neck. As cultures and societies
ⓒevolved over time, beadwork became a form of
personal expression, a symbol of social class, or
even a talisman ⓓto drive away bad luck.
Interestingly, some regions have particularly rich
traditions. The Ndebele tribe of South Africa, for
example, is famed for intricate dresses ⓔmade of
glass beads. Different designs serve as a means of
marking
different
developmental
stages
of
a
woman’s life. An unmarried girl may wear a square

A Journey to Samoa
Samoa is a Polynesian island country, ⓐconsisting
of two main islands (Upolu and Savai’i), located in
the South Pacific. It is known for its year-round
warm
tropical
weather,
stunning
beaches,
and
gorgeous waterfalls. Samoa even served as one of
the sources of inspiration for the directors of the
movie Moana released in 2016. It is a stunning
island country ⓑin which preserves its traditions,
history, and distinct way of life.
Samoans Have No Walls
A “fale” is a traditional Samoan house, with
round-shaped thatched huts, ⓒsupported by wood
columns, but with no walls. The architecture of fale
is very well-suited to the Samoan tropical climate.
(A)그것의 옆이 개방된 구조는 공기가 자유롭게 순환
하게 하여 공간을 계속 시원하게 할 뿐만 아니라 강한
바람이 빠져나갈 수 있도록 하여 그것이 극한 날씨를
견뎌낼 수 있도록 해준다. The unique structure of
the fale mirrors the Samoan people’s values of
openness and community. Its open structure allows
people ⓓcome and go freely, creating a sense of
belonging.
Samoans Were Time Travelers
Samoa
and
American
Samoa
are
different
countries, even though they are next to each other
in the South Pacific Ocean. Although these two
countries ⓔused to being in the same time zone,
the situation completely changed in 2011. On
December 29, 2011, Samoans skipped December 30,
and went straight to December 31, ⓕjumped 24
hours into the future. This happened because the
Samoan government decided to switch sides of the
International Date Line. This was ⓖto align the time
with New Zealand, Australia, and other Asian
countries, to improve their business transactions.
Samoa is now on the opposite side of the
International Date Line from American Samoa. They
are just half an hour apart by flight, but there is a
24-hour time difference between them. If you fly
from Samoa to American Samoa, in about 30
minutes you will return to yesterday!

for
stained-glass windows

quickly

buildings got bigger to accommodate more

W: Leo, what is that?
M: This is my stamp collection. I’ve collected over
700 stamps so far.
W: Amazing! Why do you collect stamps?
M: Well, I like learning about historical events through
stamp designs. For example, a Gutenberg printing
press from the 15th century is printed on this stamp.
W: A Gutenberg printing press? ______________________
_____________________
M: It was an important invention that helped people
learn how to read and write.
W: How so?
M: Before the printing press, all writings and drawings
were copied by hand. Professional copyists
worked in small rooms to copy ancient books.
W: I can’t imagine how long it must have taken to
copy an entire book by hand.
M: It took days to make a single book.
W: Books were probably too expensive for ordinary
people to own long ago.
M: Right! The printing press allowed people to make
books quickly, cheaply, and in large numbers.
W: What a revolution!

Traditionally, fishers went out to sea with fishing nets or long lines on boats to catch fish. They took advantage of their experience gained through trial and error, through observation, and through knowledge passed down from previous generations. London Transport Workers Study
In the busy London streets of 1953, a special
study was conducted. Scientists observed more than
31,000 people who had various jobs on buses and
trains. Some jobs demanded lots of moving around,
like ticket collectors, while others, like drivers, didn’t
require much movement. What was interesting was
that the workers with more active jobs had fewer
heart problems than those who sat a lot. This
implied that jobs requiring more moving around
were healthier for workers than those jobs that
didn’t. What could account for the difference in
their health outcomes?
